data.description: A benign primary cardiac tumor composed of dense collagen and fibroblasts, most often arising intramurally in the ventricular wall (especially the left ventricle).
symptoms_in_common: Single, well-circumscribed intramural mass in the left ventricle
Homogeneous, intense late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac MRI (fibrous tissue)
Echogenic, relatively avascular-appearing mass on echocardiography
Gross specimen firm, tan-white, rubbery nodule ~3–4 cm
Histology showing dense collagen with bland spindle cells and entrapped small vessels; Masson trichrome highlighting abundant collagen; no atypia/mitoses
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple myocardial nodules
Marked necrosis or hemorrhage
Infiltrative margins with destruction of adjacent myocardium

data.description: An intraventricular blood clot often forming along akinetic/dyskinetic endocardial surfaces after infarction or with severe cardiomyopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Subendocardial location along the left ventricular cavity
symptoms_not_in_common: Homogeneous intense late gadolinium enhancement (thrombus typically shows no or only peripheral enhancement)
Firm tan-white tumor-like gross specimen rather than friable clot
Histology lacking collagenous stroma and fibroblasts (thrombus would show fibrin/organization)
Well-circumscribed intramural growth (thrombus is intracavitary and mural-adherent, not intramural)

data.description: The most common benign cardiac tumor, usually arising from the left atrial septum as a pedunculated, gelatinous mass that can be mobile and embolize.
symptoms_not_in_common: Ventricular intramural location (myxomas are typically left atrial and intracavitary, attached to the fossa ovalis)
Homogeneous dense collagen on histology rather than myxoid stroma with stellate cells and hemorrhage
Firm, fibrous gross appearance instead of gelatinous, friable mass
Lack of pedunculated/mobile attachment

data.description: A benign hamartomatous tumor of cardiac muscle, most common in infants and associated with tuberous sclerosis; often multiple intramyocardial nodules.
symptoms_not_in_common: Homogeneous intense late gadolinium enhancement from dense fibrous tissue (rhabdomyomas typically show less LGE and different signal)
Single lesion rather than multiple nodules
Histology without 'spider cells' of rhabdomyoma
Firm collagenous gross specimen rather than softer muscle tumor

data.description: A rare malignant cardiac tumor that is infiltrative, often rapidly enlarging, with heterogeneous enhancement, necrosis, and histologic atypia.
symptoms_in_common: Left ventricular mass with enhancement on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Well-circumscribed, homogeneous lesion without invasion
Absence of necrosis or hemorrhage on imaging and gross exam
Histology lacking cellular atypia, high mitotic activity, or malignant vascular channels
Firm collagen-rich mass rather than heterogeneous malignant tissue

data.description: A malignant tumor of sympathetic nervous system origin, often arising from paraspinal sympathetic chain in children; may extend through the neural foramen into the spinal canal (dumbbell configuration) and shows internal vascularity and heterogeneous enhancement.
symptoms_in_common: Paraspinal soft-tissue mass adjacent to the thoracic spine on MRI
Extension through the neural foramen with intraspinal/epidural component (dumbbell configuration)
symptoms_not_in_common: No definitive calcifications demonstrated on the provided images (often present in neuroblastoma)
No clear evidence of adrenal or abdominal primary described

data.description: Neoplasms along the spectrum from malignant (ganglioneuroblastoma) to benign (ganglioneuroma) arising from sympathetic chain; commonly paraspinal, may form dumbbell masses and enhance variably.
symptoms_in_common: Thoracic paraspinal mass along sympathetic chain
Enhancing soft tissue with internal vessels on Doppler
symptoms_not_in_common: Lack of clear maturation features or well-circumscribed, homogeneous appearance typical of ganglioneuroma on imaging
No clinical data suggesting catecholamine excess provided (sometimes seen in neuroblastic tumors)

data.diagnosis: Nerve sheath tumor (schwannoma or neurofibroma) with dumbbell extension
data.description: Benign tumors arising from intercostal or spinal nerve roots; can extend through the neural foramen, forming a dumbbell shape, and often enhance on MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Paraspinal mass contiguous with neural foramen
symptoms_not_in_common: Internal vascularity on Doppler may be more than typically seen in many benign nerve sheath tumors
Age predilection often adults; pediatric occurrence is less common compared to neuroblastoma

data.description: Infectious collection adjacent to the spine that may extend into the epidural space; typically shows rim enhancement and peripheral hyperemia with systemic signs of infection.
symptoms_in_common: Paraspinal soft-tissue mass adjacent to vertebral column
symptoms_not_in_common: Internal vascular flow throughout the lesion on Doppler rather than peripheral rim flow expected for abscess
Solid, heterogeneous enhancement instead of predominant rim enhancement with central nonenhancement
No reported systemic infectious symptoms (fever, leukocytosis)
No definite vertebral body destruction or disc involvement shown

data.description: Benign proliferation of hematopoietic tissue occurring outside the marrow, often presenting as bilateral paraspinal masses in patients with chronic anemia or hemoglobinopathies.
symptoms_not_in_common: Typically bilateral and lobulated masses; images suggest a unilateral focal lesion
Usually lacks intraspinal (dumbbell) extension
Internal vascularity pattern may differ
No history of chronic anemia or hemoglobinopathy provided

data.description: A benign, congenital fluid-filled cavity in the liver, typically asymptomatic and discovered incidentally on imaging.
symptoms_in_common: CT: round, well-circumscribed low-attenuation hepatic lesion
No obvious solid components on CT image provided

data.description: Parasitic infection by Echinococcus leading to cyst formation in the liver; may show daughter cysts, septations, or calcifications.
symptoms_in_common: Potential internal complexity (possible septations/daughter cysts) suggested by cystic morphology

data.description: A bacterial infection resulting in a pus-filled cavity in the liver; often presents with fever, right upper quadrant pain, and elevated inflammatory markers.
symptoms_in_common: CT: hypodense hepatic lesion that could represent a fluid collection

data.description: Secondary liver tumors from primaries such as mucinous gastrointestinal cancers or ovarian tumors that can appear cystic or necrotic on imaging.
symptoms_in_common: CT: cystic/low-attenuation hepatic lesion compatible with necrotic or mucinous metastasis

data.description: A rare cystic tumor of the intrahepatic bile ducts that may be multilocular with septations and has malignant potential (cystadenocarcinoma).
symptoms_in_common: CT: cystic hepatic lesion that could represent a multilocular biliary cystic neoplasm

data.description: A chronic, progressive optic neuropathy characterized by retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) loss and corresponding visual field defects, often associated with elevated or fluctuating intraocular pressure but sometimes occurring with normal pressures.
symptoms_in_common: Greater thinning in inferior/temporal quadrants on OCT heat map
No acute optic disc edema on fundus photos
symptoms_not_in_common: Lack of clear disc cupping prominence on photos (pallor appears more than cupping)
No information about elevated intraocular pressure
RNFL thinning pattern could reflect optic neuritis/other optic neuropathies rather than classic glaucomatous cupping

data.diagnosis: Multiple sclerosis with prior optic neuritis
data.description: An inflammatory demyelinating disease of the central nervous system; optic neuritis is a frequent manifestation and can leave residual RNFL thinning, especially temporally, after the acute episode resolves.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral RNFL thinning on OCT consistent with previous optic nerve injury
Temporal-predominant RNFL loss (typical after optic neuritis)
No current optic disc edema (suggesting a remote episode rather than acute)
Brain and spine imaging provided for demyelinating evaluation
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear demyelinating lesions demonstrated on the provided MRI images
Asymmetry may be less typical if prior attacks were strictly unilateral
No reported history of acute painful vision loss (often present during optic neuritis)

data.diagnosis: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD)–related optic neuritis
data.description: An autoimmune astrocytopathy targeting AQP4, often causing severe, bilateral optic neuritis with marked RNFL thinning and longitudinally extensive spinal cord lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral RNFL thinning consistent with severe prior optic nerve injury
Temporal/inferior RNFL loss compatible with post-inflammatory damage
symptoms_not_in_common: Spinal MRI does not show obvious longitudinally extensive cord lesions
No acute disc edema or current severe vision loss detailed
Pattern may be milder than typically seen in NMOSD

data.description: An ischemic infarct of the anterior optic nerve head, usually in older patients, leading to altitudinal visual field loss and segmental RNFL thinning after the acute swelling resolves.
symptoms_in_common: RNFL thinning that can follow a prior ischemic event
Absence of current disc edema (suggests a past event)
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral involvement and inter-eye asymmetry rather than a classic unilateral event
Temporal-predominant thinning less typical than superior/inferior altitudinal loss
No history of acute, painless visual loss provided

data.diagnosis: Compressive optic neuropathy (e.g., chiasmal or orbital compression)
data.description: Damage to the optic nerve or chiasm from compressive lesions (pituitary adenoma, meningioma, orbital masses) leading to chronic RNFL thinning, often with temporal pallor and bitemporal field defects when chiasmal.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral RNFL thinning with temporal involvement
Chronic-appearing optic nerve changes without edema
symptoms_not_in_common: Provided MRI images do not show an obvious compressive mass
No classic bitemporal hemianopic symptoms described
RNFL loss magnitude appears modest for longstanding compression

data.diagnosis: Thoái hóa thần kinh kèm theo tích tụ sắt trong não (ví dụ: PKAN)
data.description: Một nhóm các rối loạn di truyền, đặc trưng bởi sự tích tụ sắt quá mức ở hạch đáy gây rối loạn vận động và các thay đổi đặc trưng trên MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Bất thường tín hiệu hạch nền trên MRI cho thấy sự lắng đọng kim loại nặng
symptoms_not_in_common: Vòng giác mạc Kayser–Fleischer
Đột biến ATP7B gây bệnh

data.diagnosis: Lắng đọng mangan do bệnh gan mãn tính (mangan liên quan đến bệnh não gan)
data.description: Ở rối loạn gan giai đoạn nặng, sự suy giảm khả năng loại bỏ mangan có thể gây tăng cường độ T1 ở hạch nền và các triệu chứng ngoài hình chóp.
symptoms_in_common: Tăng cường độ hạch nền T1 trên MRI tương thích với lắng đọng kim loại
symptoms_not_in_common: Vòng giác mạc Kayser–Fleischer
Biến thể gây bệnh ATP7B đã được xác nhận
Sinh thiết gan cho thấy tích tụ đồng thay vì mangan tách rời

data.diagnosis: Bệnh gan tắc mật mạn tính với tích tụ đồng thứ phát (ví dụ: viêm đường mật nguyên phát hoặc tắc mật kéo dài)
data.description: Lưu lượng mật giảm có thể gây giữ đồng thứ phát trong gan và đôi khi gây lắng đọng đồng ở giác mạc.
symptoms_in_common: Sinh thiết gan cho thấy tích tụ đồng
Khả năng lắng đọng đồng giác mạc
symptoms_not_in_common: Đột biến gây bệnh đồng hợp tử ATP7B
Thay đổi MRI hạch nền điển hình của bệnh Wilson

data.diagnosis: Phổ aceruloplasminemia/hemochromatosis (rối loạn quá tải sắt toàn thân)
data.description: Rối loạn chuyển hóa sắt di truyền dẫn đến sự lắng đỡ sắt ở nhiều cơ quan, bao gồm cả hạch nền, với các kết quả MRI đặc trưng.
symptoms_in_common: Bất thường tín hiệu hạch nền trên MRI tương thích với lắng đọng kim loại
symptoms_not_in_common: Vòng giác mạc Kayser–Fleischer
Đột biến gen ATP7B
Sinh thiết gan cho thấy lắng đọng đồng (không phải sắt)

data.description: Inflammation of the prepatellar bursa, often from repetitive kneeling or minor trauma, causing anterior knee swelling and localized tenderness; may have mild overlying erythema.
symptoms_in_common: Anterior knee swelling localized over the patella
Overlying erythema on the anterior knee
Prepatellar fullness more than circumferential joint swelling
symptoms_not_in_common: Patchy erythema extending beyond the bursa area (more suggestive of infection or cellulitis)
Marked diffuse redness down the leg

data.description: Infection of the prepatellar bursa (commonly Staphylococcus aureus), presenting with anterior knee swelling, warmth, erythema, and tenderness; may have fever and systemic symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Prominent erythema over the anterior knee
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear systemic signs provided (e.g., fever, malaise)
Erythema patches distant from the bursa could indicate broader cellulitis rather than isolated bursitis

data.description: Bacterial infection of the skin and subcutaneous tissues causing diffuse redness, warmth, swelling, and tenderness; often spreads beyond a focal structure.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse erythema around and below the knee
Ill-defined, patchy redness extending beyond the joint
symptoms_not_in_common: Discrete prepatellar bulge (more typical of bursitis)
Erythema seemingly centered over a bursal area rather than uniformly involving the limb

data.description: Infection within the knee joint causing an acutely swollen, painful, and warm joint; typically with marked limitation of motion and systemic illness.
symptoms_not_in_common: Swelling appears localized anteriorly over the patella rather than a tense circumferential joint effusion
No clear evidence of severe limitation of motion or systemic symptoms from the description
Patchy distal erythema more suggestive of cellulitis/bursitis involvement

data.diagnosis: Gout (acute gouty arthritis of the knee)
data.description: Inflammatory arthritis due to monosodium urate crystal deposition; presents with acute onset of a red, hot, swollen joint; knees can be involved though first MTP is most common.
symptoms_in_common: Red, swollen knee consistent with acute inflammatory arthritis
symptoms_not_in_common: Predominantly prepatellar localization rather than a classic intra-articular effusion
Patchy erythema extending down the leg (not typical of isolated gout)
No history of sudden severe joint pain provided

data.description: Acute inflammatory arthritis due to calcium pyrophosphate crystals; often affects larger joints like the knee and mimics gout or septic arthritis.
symptoms_in_common: Appearance of inflammatory process in a large joint
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent prepatellar soft-tissue swelling suggesting bursal involvement more than intra-articular effusion
Patchy, spreading skin erythema (more typical of cellulitis or septic bursitis)
No reported sudden severe joint pain or known chondrocalcinosis

data.description: A deep neck space infection located in the retropharyngeal space that can contain pus and gas, potentially life‑threatening due to airway compromise and mediastinal spread.
symptoms_in_common: Prevertebral soft tissue swelling on CT
Potential mucosal disruption suggesting source of infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Presence of tracheostomy tube (not typical cause; more a consequence or unrelated device)

data.description: A tear or rupture of the cervical esophagus leading to extraluminal air and potential infection in the retropharyngeal or prevertebral spaces.
symptoms_in_common: Possible linear foreign body or mucosal breach along hypopharynx/esophagus
symptoms_not_in_common: Tracheostomy tube present (not a typical feature, though it may coexist)
No provided history of caustic ingestion or recent endoscopic procedure

data.diagnosis: Ingested fish bone impaction (hypopharynx/cervical esophagus) with secondary soft‑tissue emphysema
data.description: A sharp, radiopaque foreign body (often fish bone) lodged in the hypopharynx or upper esophagus that can cause local perforation and introduce air into deep neck spaces.
symptoms_in_common: Linear radiodense object/defect compatible with foreign body
symptoms_not_in_common: Tracheostomy tube present (not typical for initial presentation)

data.diagnosis: Necrotizing soft tissue infection of the neck (necrotizing fasciitis)
data.description: A rapidly progressive infection causing soft‑tissue necrosis, often with gas formation in fascial planes; can arise from pharyngeal or dental sources and spread along deep neck spaces.
symptoms_in_common: Gas within deep neck spaces on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Clear focal foreign body (not a typical requirement, though can be a trigger)
Tracheostomy tube (not a typical primary feature)

data.description: Disruption of laryngeal or hypopharyngeal structures due to trauma (including iatrogenic injury) that can introduce air into adjacent spaces and cause swelling.
symptoms_in_common: Possible mucosal disruption or linear defect compatible with trauma
symptoms_not_in_common: No explicit history of external trauma provided
Tracheostomy tube present (may be a management step rather than a primary feature)

A neuroendocrine tumor of pancreatic beta cells causing autonomous insulin secretion and recurrent fasting hypoglycemia.
Hypoglycemia due to ingestion of insulin secretagogues (e.g., sulfonylureas) that stimulate endogenous insulin release.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated C-peptide (3.214 nmol/L) indicating endogenous secretion

data.description: Diffuse beta-cell hyperfunction (often post–bariatric surgery) causing inappropriate insulin secretion and fasting or postprandial hypoglycemia.
Autoantibodies bind endogenous insulin, causing episodes of hypoglycemia with elevated total insulin; often triggered by certain drugs or occurring in predisposed individuals.
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated C-peptide (3.214 nmol/L) — C-peptide is often normal or low in classic insulin autoimmune syndrome

data.description: Use of injected insulin leading to hypoglycemia; typically associated with high insulin levels and suppressed ketogenesis.
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated C-peptide (3.214 nmol/L) — exogenous insulin usually suppresses endogenous C-peptide (expected low/normal)

data.description: Metabolic bone disease in children caused by inadequate vitamin D leading to defective mineralization of the growth plate and bone, often producing a rachitic rosary (beading of costochondral junctions).
symptoms_in_common: Beading/enlargement of costochondral junctions (rachitic rosary) on ultrasound
Multiple adjacent ribs (7th–9th) involved with anterior rib-end prominence

data.diagnosis: Renal osteodystrophy with secondary hyperparathyroidism (calcipenic rickets)
data.description: Bone changes from chronic kidney disease and secondary hyperparathyroidism causing defective mineralization and rickets-like changes in growing children.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple rib involvement compatible with metabolic bone disease

data.description: Inherited or acquired renal phosphate loss causing hypophosphatemia, impaired mineralization, and rickets in children.
symptoms_in_common: Rachitic rosary appearance with enlarged anterior rib ends

data.diagnosis: Scurvy (vitamin C deficiency) with scorbutic rosary
data.description: Deficiency of vitamin C leading to impaired collagen synthesis; in children can cause a scorbutic rosary (prominence at costochondral junctions) though typically sharper and with adjacent depression.
symptoms_in_common: Prominent costochondral junctions on rib ultrasound

data.description: Benign, self-limited inflammation of a single costochondral junction, usually in the upper ribs, causing localized swelling and pain.
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple adjacent ribs (7th–9th) involved rather than a single focal upper rib lesion

data.description: Presence of multiple gas-filled cysts within the submucosa or subserosa of the bowel wall; often benign/idiopathic or secondary to other gastrointestinal or pulmonary conditions.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple polypoid, submucosal bleb-like lesions on colonoscopy
Radiographic intramural radiolucent collections consistent with gas (‘grape-like’/thumbprinting appearance)
Endoscopic ultrasound showing highly reflective interfaces with posterior acoustic shadowing compatible with gas
Histology demonstrating empty submucosal cystic spaces with macrophage/giant-cell lining (CD68-positive)
symptoms_not_in_common: Ulceration with active purulent exudate
Diffuse mucosal friability typical of inflammatory bowel disease
Severe systemic toxicity or sepsis

data.description: Benign condition characterized by mucin-filled cysts in the submucosa due to mucosal herniation, often in the rectum; can mimic neoplasm endoscopically.
symptoms_in_common: Cystic spaces within submucosa on endoscopic ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: Histology shows mucin pools lined by epithelium rather than empty gas-filled cysts with CD68-positive histiocytes
Lack of intramural gas on radiograph (patient shows radiolucent gas collections)
Typical localization to rectum rather than more diffuse colonic involvement

data.description: Benign vascular malformation of lymphatic channels forming submucosal cystic lesions; can present as multiple translucent polypoid masses.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple smooth submucosal, cystic-appearing lesions on colonoscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Radiographic evidence of intramural gas (not typical for lymphangioma)
Histology lacking lymphatic endothelium and chyle; instead shows empty spaces with macrophages/giant cells consistent with gas
EUS in lymphangioma usually shows anechoic fluid-filled spaces without strong echogenic shadowing from gas

data.description: Transient or persistent colonic ischemia causing mucosal edema, hemorrhage, and possible ulceration; commonly presents with abdominal pain and hematochezia.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging can show thumbprinting from submucosal edema
symptoms_not_in_common: Presence of gas-filled submucosal cysts on endoscopy/EUS
Histology showing empty cysts with CD68-positive histiocytes rather than ischemic necrosis and hemorrhage
Absence of reported acute abdominal pain or hematochezia

data.diagnosis: Emphysematous colitis (infectious/necrotizing colitis with intramural gas)
data.description: Severe, often life-threatening colitis due to gas-forming organisms leading to intramural gas with systemic toxicity.
symptoms_not_in_common: Systemic toxicity (fever, leukocytosis, sepsis) typically present but not reported
Ulceronecrotic mucosa rather than smooth polypoid blebs
Histology in patient shows benign-appearing gas cysts with macrophages, not fulminant necrosis

data.description: La bioquímica de la sangre periférica mostró eosinofilia (eosinófilos 53,5%, leucocitos 7.700/μL) con anemia (Hgb 8,6 g/dL, glóbulos rojos 3,66 ×10^6/μL). La PCR estaba ligeramente elevada a 2,66 mg/dL. La función renal y hepática fue en gran medida normal (BUN 12,0 mg/dL, creatinina 0,90 mg/dL, AST 15 U/L, ALT 11 U/L). ANA, RF, anticuerpo Jo-1, PR-ANCA, MPO-ANCA fueron negativos; HBsAg, HBsAb, HCV Ab y HIV Ab fueron negativos. La gasometría arterial mostró pH 7,549, pCO2 27,1 mmHg, pO2 68,2 mmHg y HCO3 23,1 mmol/L. Otros valores notables incluyeron IgE 254 IU/mL y receptor soluble IL-2 495 U/mL.
Una neoplasia mieloide clonal caracterizada por hipereosinofilia persistente con evidencia de clonalidad mieloide y ausencia de PDGFRA/PDGFRB/FGFR1 u otros reordenamientos definitorios.
symptoms_in_common: Presencia de precursores eosinófilos (mielocitos/metamielocitos) en la citología
symptoms_not_in_common: Megaloblastos y neutrófilos hipersegmentados (sugieren cambios megaloblásticos, no es clásico para el CEL)
Alcalosis respiratoria con hipoxemia (no es una característica definitoria; podría representar un proceso pulmonar no relacionado)

data.description: Un trastorno clonal de la médula ósea con displasia y citopenias; algunos casos presentan eosinofilia periférica y anomalías citogenéticas como pérdida o ganancia de 1q.
symptoms_in_common: Anemia con características displásicas (megaloblastos, neutrófilos hipersegmentados)
Eosinofilia con formas eosinófilas inmaduras en el frotis
Anomalías citogenéticas que afectan a los cromosomas 1 y 7
symptoms_not_in_common: IgE elevada (no típica del MDS)
Alcalosis respiratoria con hipoxemia (no es un rasgo típico de la presentación)

data.diagnosis: Neoplasia mieloide/linfoide con eosinofilia y reorganización de tirosina quinasa (por ejemplo, PDGFRA/PDGFRB/FGFR1)
data.description: Neoplasias mieloides impulsadas por fusión que presentan hipereosinofilia; a menudo responden a inhibidores de tirosina quinasa dependiendo de la reorganización.
symptoms_in_common: Análisis normales de hígado y riñón
symptoms_not_in_common: Anomalías del cariotipo observadas en los cromosomas 1 y 7 en lugar de los loci clásicos (4q12 PDGFRA, 5q33 PDGFRB, 8p11 FGFR1)
Cambios megaloblásticos (no típicos)
Índice de IgE y IL-2 soluble elevado (no característico)

data.diagnosis: Síndrome idiopático hipereosinofílico (HES), posible variante linfocítica
data.description: Un trastorno con eosinofilia sostenida (>1500/μL) que causa afectación de órganos; la variante linfocítica está impulsada por células T productoras de IL-5 y a menudo muestra IgE elevada y receptores solubles de IL-2.
symptoms_in_common: Hipoxemia que podría reflejar afectación pulmonar
Serologías autoinmunes negativas y cribados virales
symptoms_not_in_common: Presencia de anomalías citogenéticas clonales (argumenta en contra de la HES puramente idiopática)
Megaloblastos y neutrófilos hipersegmentados que sugieren cambios megaloblásticos
Anemia (no es típica salvo que sea por causas secundarias)

data.diagnosis: Infección parasitaria helmintica (por ejemplo, strongiloidiasis o anquilostomícola)
data.description: Las infecciones parasitarias suelen causar eosinofilia; el anquilostomas puede causar anemia por pérdida de sangre, y algunos helmintos elevan la IgE.
symptoms_not_in_common: Anomalías citogenéticas (no esperadas en la infección)
Presencia de precursores eosinófilos en el frotis sanguíneo
Megaloblastos y neutrófilos hipersegmentados
No se proporciona historial negativo de viajes/parásitos; función normal de hígado/riñón
Receptor soluble de IL-2 elevado (no típico)

data.diagnosis: Anemia megaloblástica debida a deficiencia de vitamina B12 o folato
data.description: Deficiencia de vitamina B12 o folato que causa hematopoyesis ineficaz, macrocitosis, neutrófilos hipersegmentados y anemia.
symptoms_not_in_common: Eosinofilia marcada (no típica de deficiencia aislada de B12/folato)
IgE elevado y receptor soluble de IL-2 (no esperado)
Anomalías citogenéticas (no parte de la deficiencia nutricional)
Hipoxemia y alcalosis respiratoria (no relacionadas)

data.diagnosis: Rosai–Dorfman disease (sinus histiocytosis with massive lymphadenopathy) with gastrointestinal involvement
data.description: A benign histiocytic proliferative disorder characterized by S100+/CD68+ histiocytes showing emperipolesis and typically CD1a negative; can present with nodal and extranodal disease, including bowel lesions that can act as a lead point for intussusception.
symptoms_in_common: Bowel-within-bowel (target) sign on ultrasound consistent with intussusception
Ileocecal mass with mesenteric lymphadenopathy on CT
Histology showing large histiocytes with emperipolesis
Immunophenotype: S100 positive, CD68/CD163 positive, CD1a negative
symptoms_not_in_common: Very high tumor proliferation index (Ki-67 near 100%) is not typical
B-cell markers (CD20, CD10) would not be expected

data.description: An aggressive B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma commonly involving the ileocecal region in children; rapidly growing mass can cause intussusception and marked FDG avidity.
symptoms_in_common: Ileocecal mass causing intussusception on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Histology does not show classic starry-sky pattern with high mitotic rate
Immunophenotype lacks B-cell markers (CD20/CD10) and shows S100+/CD68+ histiocytes instead
CD1a negativity and emperipolesis are not typical for Burkitt lymphoma

data.description: Clonal proliferation of Langerhans cells that can involve the GI tract; lesions may be FDG-avid and produce masses or strictures that could precipitate intussusception.
symptoms_in_common: Possible bowel involvement that can serve as a lead point for intussusception
symptoms_not_in_common: Expected immunophenotype would be CD1a and Langerin (CD207) positive; case shows CD1a negative
Emperipolesis is not a feature of Langerhans cells
Typical skeletal or skin lesions are not described

data.diagnosis: Meckel’s diverticulum or enteric duplication cyst acting as a lead point
data.description: Congenital anomalies of the distal ileum that can act as a lead point for ileo-ileal or ileocecal intussusception in children.
symptoms_in_common: Localized ileal process near the ileocecal region
symptoms_not_in_common: Lack of cystic lesion or diverticulum identified on imaging
Presence of widespread mesenteric lymphadenopathy and FDG-avid nodal/soft-tissue lesions is atypical
Histology shows histiocytic proliferation rather than ectopic gastric mucosa or duplication cyst wall

data.diagnosis: Inflammatory fibroid polyp (Vanek tumor) of the ileum/ileocecum
data.description: A rare benign submucosal lesion composed of spindle cells and eosinophils that can occur in the small bowel and act as a lead point for intussusception.
symptoms_in_common: Discrete intraluminal mass as potential lead point
symptoms_not_in_common: Extensive nodal disease and splenic/hepatic lesions are unusual
PET uptake pattern and histology with S100+/CD68+ histiocytes and emperipolesis do not match spindle-cell inflammatory fibroid polyp histology
CD1a negativity with histiocytic markers does not fit this diagnosis

diagnoses.name: Mixed-cellularity subtype of classic Hodgkin's lymphoma
diagnoses.title: Mixed cellularity classical Hodgkin lymphoma

data.description: Initial evaluation showed severe thrombocytopenia (platelets 24,000/µL) with leukocytosis with neutrophilia and lymphopenia, elevated hemoglobin/hematocrit, mild hyponatremia, hypochloremia, elevated creatinine, hypomagnesemia, elevated transaminases, hyperbilirubinemia, and very low haptoglobin.

A life-threatening parasitic infection of red blood cells that can cause hemolysis, thrombocytopenia, hepatic dysfunction, and acute kidney injury; confirmed by rapid diagnostic test and peripheral smear with ring forms.
symptoms_in_common: evidence of intravascular hemolysis (very low haptoglobin)
peripheral smear with intraerythrocytic ring forms
symptoms_not_in_common: leukocytosis with neutrophilia (malaria often has normal/low WBC)
elevated hemoglobin/hematocrit (malaria more often causes anemia)

data.description: A thrombotic microangiopathy due to ADAMTS13 deficiency causing platelet consumption and microangiopathic hemolytic anemia with possible neurologic and renal involvement.
symptoms_not_in_common: positive malaria test and intraerythrocytic parasites
elevated hemoglobin/hematocrit (TTP usually shows anemia)
marked leukocytosis is not classic
transaminase elevation is not typical

data.description: A thrombotic microangiopathy often triggered by Shiga-toxin–producing organisms leading to hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and acute kidney injury.
symptoms_in_common: evidence of hemolysis (very low haptoglobin, hyperbilirubinemia)
symptoms_not_in_common: positive malaria tests and parasites on smear
elevated hemoglobin/hematocrit (HUS typically has anemia)
significant transaminase elevation not typical
leukocytosis with neutrophilia not a hallmark

data.description: A viral infection causing capillary leak and thrombocytopenia; can present with hemoconcentration, transaminitis, and hyponatremia.
symptoms_not_in_common: very low haptoglobin (hemolysis is not typical in dengue)
hyperbilirubinemia is less common
leukocytosis with neutrophilia (dengue usually has leukopenia)
positive malaria tests/smear
elevated creatinine not typical unless severe dehydration/shock

data.description: A tick-borne intraerythrocytic parasitic infection causing hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia, clinically similar to malaria.
symptoms_in_common: evidence of hemolysis (very low haptoglobin, hyperbilirubinemia)
symptoms_not_in_common: positive falciparum-specific rapid test and smear morphology favor malaria over Babesia
elevated hemoglobin/hematocrit (Babesiosis usually causes anemia)
leukocytosis with neutrophilia is not typical

data.description: A systemic inflammatory response to infection causing coagulopathy, platelet consumption, organ dysfunction, and potential hemolysis.
symptoms_not_in_common: positive malaria rapid test and parasitemia on smear (points to malaria etiology rather than primary bacterial sepsis)
elevated hemoglobin/hematocrit is atypical for sepsis
lymphopenia is not specific

data.description: A tear of the cervical esophagus, often due to instrumentation or procedures, leading to leakage of secretions/contrast and secondary infection of the mediastinum.
symptoms_in_common: Endoscopic visualization of pus tracking into the mediastinum
Contrast leak on esophagram into mediastinum
Visible defect near the upper esophageal sphincter

data.description: Full-thickness esophageal rupture typically after forceful emesis, causing mediastinal contamination and severe infection.
symptoms_in_common: Pus and mediastinal contamination on endoscopy
Need for endoscopic stent to control leak

data.diagnosis: Hypopharyngeal (pyriform sinus) perforation with descending mediastinitis
data.description: A perforation of the hypopharynx (e.g., pyriform sinus) that allows oropharyngeal secretions to track into the mediastinum, causing infection.
symptoms_in_common: Findings localized near upper esophageal sphincter/arytenoid region

data.diagnosis: Esophageal perforation due to foreign body
data.description: A sharp or impacted foreign body causes a transmural tear of the esophagus, leading to leakage and mediastinitis.
symptoms_in_common: Need for endoscopic intervention and stenting

data.description: A pharyngoesophageal diverticulum arising above the upper esophageal sphincter that can rarely perforate or leak, leading to infection.
symptoms_in_common: Pathology centered at the upper esophageal sphincter/hypopharyngeal area
Leakage of contrast/secretions with mediastinal contamination

data.description: Infected pleural fluid collection that often follows bacterial pneumonia; characterized by loculated pleural fluid, pleural thickening/enhancement, and adjacent lung consolidation.
symptoms_in_common: Pleural thickening with split-pleura appearance on CT
Air within the pleural collection (possible gas-forming organisms or bronchopleural fistula)
symptoms_not_in_common: Large free pleural air producing a classic hydropneumothorax (empyema usually fluid-dominant unless fistula present)

data.description: Simultaneous pleural air and fluid caused by a communication between the bronchial tree and pleural space; may occur after necrotizing pneumonia, ruptured lung abscess, or surgery/trauma.
symptoms_in_common: Signs of prior/parapneumonic infection in the adjacent lobe
symptoms_not_in_common: Extensive pleural thickening and loculations (more suggestive of empyema)
Uniform large-volume effusion without air

data.description: Localized necrotizing infection of lung parenchyma causing a cavity with an air-fluid level; often communicates with bronchi and may cause an associated reactive or infected pleural effusion.
symptoms_in_common: Cavitary process with air-fluid characteristics near the pleural surface
symptoms_not_in_common: Dominant pleural air-fluid level suggesting pleural rather than intraparenchymal cavity
Extensive pleural thickening/split-pleura sign (more typical of empyema)

data.diagnosis: Malignant pleural effusion with trapped lung
data.description: Pleural fluid accumulation caused by pleural metastasis or mesothelioma; can lead to a nonexpanding lung and pleural thickening.
symptoms_not_in_common: Pleural gas or clear air-fluid level (unusual without prior thoracentesis or fistula)
Prominent adjacent acute consolidation suggestive of infection

data.diagnosis: Tuberculous pleurisy with secondary empyema (possibly with bronchopleural fistula)
data.description: Mycobacterial infection involving the pleura causing exudative effusion that can become chronic and infected; chronic cases may form empyema and fistulae with pleural air.
symptoms_not_in_common: Overt acute lobar consolidation typical of bacterial pneumonia rather than classic subacute TB pattern
Lack of apical cavitary parenchymal disease on the provided images

data.description: A severe developmental epileptic encephalopathy characterized by multiple seizure types, cognitive/behavioral impairment, and a characteristic EEG with generalized slow spike-and-wave (~1.5–2.5 Hz) and paroxysmal fast activity.
symptoms_in_common: EEG: generalized slow spike-and-wave discharges (~2 Hz)
High-amplitude, diffuse discharges with frontal predominance
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported history of multiple seizure types (e.g., atonic/drop attacks, tonic, atypical absence)
No reported developmental delay or cognitive impairment
No clinical seizure semiology provided to correlate with EEG

data.description: An idiopathic generalized epilepsy presenting in school-age children with brief staring spells and a classic EEG pattern of generalized 3-Hz spike-and-wave bursts.
symptoms_not_in_common: Spike-and-wave frequency appears slower than the classic 3 Hz
No reported brief staring spells with abrupt onset/offset
No hyperventilation-provoked episodes reported

data.description: A common idiopathic generalized epilepsy with myoclonic jerks, often on awakening, and EEG showing generalized 4–6 Hz polyspike-and-wave discharges.
symptoms_in_common: Generalized, symmetric discharges suggesting idiopathic generalized epilepsy
symptoms_not_in_common: EEG lacks typical 4–6 Hz polyspike-and-wave pattern
No reported morning myoclonic jerks
No history of triggers such as sleep deprivation or photic sensitivity provided

data.diagnosis: Absence status epilepticus (nonconvulsive status epilepticus of generalized onset)
data.description: Prolonged or repeated absence activity leading to continuous or near-continuous impaired responsiveness with generalized spike-and-wave on EEG.
symptoms_in_common: Slow spike-and-wave possible in atypical/absence status contexts
symptoms_not_in_common: No report of prolonged confusion or fluctuating responsiveness
No clinical correlation of continuous behavioral arrest provided
No documented precipitating factors (e.g., medication changes)

data.description: Inflammation of a congenital true diverticulum arising from the antimesenteric border of the distal ileum; can mimic appendicitis and may cause obstruction from inflammation, volvulus around a fibrous band, or intussusception.
symptoms_in_common: CT: blind-ending outpouching arising from distal ileum
CT: surrounding fat stranding and wall thickening consistent with inflammation
CT: dilated proximal small-bowel loops suggesting obstruction/transition point
symptoms_not_in_common: CT: clear inflamed appendix contiguous with cecum (not seen)
CT: diffuse terminal ileitis without focal diverticulum

data.description: Inflammation of the vermiform appendix, typically arising from the cecal base; presents with right lower quadrant pain and can have a blind-ending inflamed tubular structure on imaging.
symptoms_in_common: CT: blind-ending tubular structure with surrounding fat stranding
symptoms_not_in_common: CT: tubular structure appears to arise from distal ileum rather than the cecal base
CT: antimesenteric outpouching morphology suggestive of diverticulum rather than appendix
CT: prominent small-bowel diverticulum identified
CT: significant small-bowel obstruction (less typical in uncomplicated appendicitis)

data.description: Inflammation of acquired small-bowel diverticula, usually on the mesenteric border and often multiple; can cause localized inflammatory changes and, less commonly, obstruction or perforation.
symptoms_in_common: CT: inflamed blind-ending outpouching from small bowel
CT: peridiverticular fat stranding and wall thickening
symptoms_not_in_common: CT: solitary antimesenteric distal ileal diverticulum (more consistent with Meckel than acquired diverticula)
CT: location near terminal ileum rather than typical jejunal predominance

data.description: Chronic transmural inflammatory bowel disease commonly involving the terminal ileum; can present with segmental ileitis, strictures, and obstruction.
symptoms_not_in_common: CT: focal antimesenteric diverticulum (not typical of Crohn's)
CT: absence of long-segment mural thickening, stratification, creeping fat, or skip lesions

data.diagnosis: Small-bowel obstruction due to adhesive band or other mechanical cause (non-diverticular)
data.description: Mechanical obstruction of the small intestine, commonly from postoperative adhesions, hernias, or masses; presents with dilated proximal loops and a transition point.
symptoms_in_common: CT: dilated small-bowel loops with a transition point indicating obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: CT: identifiable inflamed distal ileal diverticulum suggesting a specific cause (Meckel) rather than idiopathic adhesions
CT: lack of clear adhesive band or hernia on imaging

An autoimmune microangiopathy that causes branch retinal artery occlusions (BRAOs), encephalopathy with characteristic corpus callosum lesions, and sensorineural hearing loss.
symptoms_in_common: Branch retinal artery occlusion on fundus/fluorescein angiography
Visual field defects consistent with sectoral retinal ischemia
MRI showing diffusion-restricted lesions in the corpus callosum ('snowball' lesions)
Unilateral sensorineural hearing loss on audiogram
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear encephalopathy or cognitive symptoms reported (often present in Susac)

data.diagnosis: Primary angiitis of the central nervous system (PACNS) with ocular involvement
data.description: Inflammation of small- to medium-sized cerebral vessels that can cause multifocal brain ischemia and, less commonly, retinal arterial occlusions; may also affect the inner ear vasculature.
symptoms_in_common: Multifocal ischemic-appearing brain lesions on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Lack of systemic inflammatory signs or other organ involvement
Typical angiographic or biopsy evidence not provided

data.description: A hypercoagulable disorder that causes arterial and venous thrombosis, which can involve retinal arteries and cerebral circulation; inner ear ischemia can lead to sensorineural hearing loss.
symptoms_in_common: MRI evidence suggestive of ischemic brain lesions
Sensorineural hearing loss possibly ischemic in origin
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of thrombosis elsewhere, pregnancy morbidity, or laboratory evidence of antiphospholipid antibodies provided
Corpus callosum-centered lesions are less characteristic than in Susac

data.diagnosis: Multiple sclerosis (MS) with coincident retinal ischemia
data.description: A demyelinating disease of the CNS that can produce callosal lesions and visual field defects from optic pathway involvement; retinal ischemia would be atypical but possible if coexisting vascular event occurs.
symptoms_in_common: MRI lesions involving the corpus callosum
symptoms_not_in_common: Branch retinal artery occlusion is not typical for MS (MS more often causes optic neuritis with optic disc/nerve findings)
Sensorineural hearing loss is less common and not a classic MS triad finding

data.diagnosis: Embolic branch retinal artery occlusion with unrelated sensorineural hearing loss
data.description: A focal retinal ischemic event from emboli (e.g., carotid or cardiac) causing sectoral retinal whitening and corresponding visual field loss; hearing loss could be due to another otologic cause.
symptoms_in_common: Fundus and fluorescein findings consistent with branch retinal artery occlusion
symptoms_not_in_common: MRI callosal lesions not explained by isolated ocular emboli
Concurrent sensorineural hearing loss not accounted for by a purely ocular embolic event

data.diagnosis: Mitochondrial myopathy (e.g., MERRF spectrum or mitochondrial cytopathy)
data.description: A group of disorders caused by defects in mitochondrial DNA or nuclear genes affecting oxidative phosphorylation; classically shows ragged‑red fibers and COX‑negative fibers with multisystem involvement such as myopathy and seizures.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated serum CK in some relatives
Muscle biopsy with ragged‑red fibers and COX‑negative fibers
symptoms_not_in_common: Pedigree appears autosomal dominant rather than maternal inheritance
No clear lactic acidosis or stroke‑like episodes reported
Hashimoto thyroiditis is not a classic feature

data.description: An autosomal dominant myopathy characterized by aggregation of desmin and other proteins leading to progressive muscle weakness, often with early axial/paraspinal involvement causing camptocormia; CK can be mildly to moderately elevated.
symptoms_in_common: Adult onset axial weakness with bent spine
symptoms_not_in_common: Muscle biopsy described with ragged‑red/COX‑negative fibers rather than desmin‑positive protein aggregates or rimmed vacuoles
Seizures and brain MRI changes are not typical of desminopathy

data.description: A common autosomal dominant muscular dystrophy due to D4Z4 repeat contraction or SMCHD1 variants; presents with slowly progressive weakness that often involves facial, scapular, and truncal muscles and can include paraspinal weakness with camptocormia.
symptoms_in_common: Adult-onset truncal/paraspinal weakness with bent spine
symptoms_not_in_common: No facial or scapular winging reported
Muscle biopsy shows mitochondrial changes rather than dystrophic changes with inflammatory infiltrates
Seizures and brain MRI changes are uncommon in FSHD

data.description: An autosomal recessive metabolic myopathy causing glycogen accumulation; presents with proximal and axial weakness, paraspinal involvement leading to bent spine, and respiratory muscle weakness; CK can be elevated.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated CK reported in family members
symptoms_not_in_common: Inheritance appears autosomal dominant rather than recessive
Muscle biopsy lacks PAS‑positive glycogen-filled vacuoles typical of Pompe disease
Seizures and brain MRI abnormalities are not typical for Pompe disease

data.diagnosis: Burkitt lymphoma/leukemia (mature B‑cell neoplasm with MYC rearrangement)
data.description: Aggressive mature B‑cell lymphoma often presenting with bone marrow and blood involvement; characterized by MYC translocation, extremely high proliferation, and monomorphic medium-sized cells.
symptoms_in_common: Very high proliferation index on immunohistochemistry (Ki‑67 approaching 100%)
Sheets of monomorphic lymphoid cells in marrow/biopsy
Cytology with deeply basophilic cytoplasm and vacuolation compatible with Burkitt morphology
Conventional karyotype showing abnormality involving chromosome 8 and 14 consistent with t(8;14)(q24;q32)
symptoms_not_in_common: Sustained strong BCL2 expression (Burkitt classically BCL2 negative)
Pronounced pleomorphism and variable cell size (Burkitt is typically monomorphic)
Absence of MYC rearrangement (required for definitive Burkitt diagnosis)
TdT positivity (Burkitt is a mature B‑cell neoplasm and TdT negative)

data.diagnosis: High‑grade B‑cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangements (double‑/triple‑hit lymphoma)
data.description: A very aggressive lymphoma showing MYC plus BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangements; overlaps morphologically with Burkitt and diffuse large B‑cell lymphoma and often presents with high tumor burden and marrow involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Very high proliferation index on IHC
Diffuse marrow/biopsy infiltration by high‑grade B‑cells
Complex karyotype with multiple abnormalities in addition to 8q24 (MYC) and 14q32 (IGH) involvement
FISH signal pattern compatible with MYC rearrangement; potential additional hits
symptoms_not_in_common: Classic isolated t(8;14) without additional BCL2/BCL6 hits (would favor Burkitt)
Uniform medium cell size with classic Burkitt morphology (double‑hit often shows more pleomorphism)
Complete absence of BCL2 expression (double‑hit commonly BCL2 positive)

data.diagnosis: Diffuse large B‑cell lymphoma (DLBCL), germinal‑center B‑cell type
data.description: The most common aggressive B‑cell lymphoma; GCB subtype often expresses CD10/BCL6 and has high proliferation; may secondarily acquire MYC rearrangements but not obligatory.
symptoms_in_common: Germinal center immunophenotype suggested by CD10/BCL6 positivity on IHC (if present in panels)
Possibility of MYC rearrangement in a subset (secondary MYC)
symptoms_not_in_common: Obligate MYC/IGH translocation (not required for DLBCL)
Classic Burkitt monomorphic medium‑sized cells with ‘starry sky’ pattern
Complete lack of BCL2 expression (DLBCL often expresses BCL2)

data.description: Neoplasm of precursor B‑cells typically TdT positive; presents with marrow blasts and high proliferation; cytogenetics vary and may show complex abnormalities but do not require MYC/IGH.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse bone marrow replacement by blasts
Cytology of blast-like cells on smears
Complex karyotype with multiple chromosomal abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Definitive MYC/IGH fusion (not typical for B‑ALL; suggests mature B‑cell process)
Mature B‑cell phenotype with surface light chain restriction (B‑ALL is precursor and TdT positive)
Classic Burkitt morphology and BCL6 positivity (B‑ALL usually lacks BCL6 and expresses TdT)

diagnoses.name: B-cell lymphoma, unclassifiable, with features intermediate between diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and Burkitt lymphoma
diagnoses.title: B-cell lymphoma unclassifiable with features intermediate between Burkitt lymphoma and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma

data.description: Bacterial infection of the liver resulting in one or more pus-filled cavities, often arising from biliary tract infection, portal seeding, or hematogenous spread.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple low-attenuation hepatic lesions on CT
Possible rim enhancement of lesions on contrast CT
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever reported (not provided)
No right upper quadrant pain reported (not provided)
No leukocytosis reported (not provided)

data.description: Hepatic abscess caused by Entamoeba histolytica; usually solitary and in the right lobe but may be multiple, especially in some presentations.
symptoms_in_common: Heterogeneous hypoechoic liver lesion(s) on ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of dysentery or travel to endemic regions reported (not provided)
No fever or right upper quadrant pain reported (not provided)
Multiplicity of lesions is less typical for classic amoebic abscess

data.description: Secondary malignant tumors of the liver from a primary cancer elsewhere; commonly present as multiple hypovascular or hypervascular lesions depending on primary.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple hypodense liver lesions on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: No known primary malignancy reported (not provided)
No weight loss or systemic cancer-related symptoms reported (not provided)

data.description: Benign vascular tumors of the liver; can be multiple; typically show peripheral nodular enhancement with progressive fill-in on contrast imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Hypodense lesions on non-contrast/portal venous CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Classic peripheral nodular enhancement with centripetal fill-in not specified (imaging pattern not provided)
No symptoms (often asymptomatic) vs. hepatomegaly present here

data.description: Primary or secondary hepatic lymphoma presenting with diffuse infiltration or multiple hypodense lesions, often with hepatomegaly and sometimes splenomegaly.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple low-attenuation hepatic lesions on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: No B-symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss) reported (not provided)
No lymphadenopathy reported (not provided)

data.description: Parasitic infection by Echinococcus leading to cystic hepatic lesions which may show daughter cysts, calcifications, or heterogeneous contents if complicated.
symptoms_not_in_common: Typical cystic appearance with daughter cysts or calcified rim not clearly described
No exposure/travel or animal contact history reported (not provided)
No eosinophilia reported (not provided)

data.description: Transmural myocardial infarction due to occlusion of the left anterior descending artery, producing localized ischemia/injury in the anterior-septal/lateral walls.
symptoms_in_common: Localized ST-segment elevation in precordial leads (V3–V6)
Very tall, broad-based (hyperacute) T waves in anterior/precordial leads
Sinus rhythm without significant PR depression
Absence of pathologic Q waves (consistent with very early phase)
symptoms_not_in_common: Lack of clear reciprocal ST-segment depression in opposing leads (can be absent early but not typical later)

data.description: Elevated serum potassium causes characteristic ECG changes progressing from peaked T waves to conduction widening and arrhythmias.
symptoms_in_common: Relatively narrow QRS complexes (compatible with early hyperkalemia)
symptoms_not_in_common: Peaked T waves are localized rather than diffuse
Presence of localized ST-segment elevation (not typical for hyperkalemia)
No PR prolongation or QRS widening seen (expected as K+ rises)

data.description: A non-ischemic variant with J-point elevation and concave ST elevation, often seen in young/healthy individuals.
symptoms_in_common: ST-segment elevation predominantly in precordial leads
symptoms_not_in_common: T waves appear very tall/broad (more suggestive of hyperacute ischemia)
Apparent localization rather than a stable, diffuse pattern
Absence of clear J-point notching/slurring in multiple leads

data.description: Inflammation of the pericardium causing diffuse ST elevation and PR-segment depression.
symptoms_not_in_common: ST elevation is not diffuse (mainly anterior/precordial)
No PR-segment depression noted
Tall hyperacute-appearing T waves (pericarditis usually has more modest ST changes and later T-wave inversion)

data.description: Transient focal coronary artery spasm causing episodic transmural ischemia with temporary ST elevation.
symptoms_in_common: Localized ST-segment elevation in precordial leads
Prominent, hyperacute-appearing T waves during episodes
Potential absence of Q waves if transient
symptoms_not_in_common: ECG may not show the transient nature in a single snapshot
Lack of clinical context of episodic rest pain or reversibility

diagnoses.title: Acute ST segment elevation myocardial infarction

data.description: A congenital, nonfunctioning segment of lung that lacks normal bronchial communication and receives arterial blood supply from the systemic circulation (usually the aorta). Can present in neonates with respiratory distress and a posterior basal mass; may be intralobar or extralobar.
symptoms_in_common: unilateral posterior-basal lung mass/opacity on chest radiograph
systemic arterial feeder seen on Doppler/CT arising from aorta
symptoms_not_in_common: mediastinal shift to the contralateral side is less typical unless lesion is large
diffuse bilateral lung disease

data.description: A developmental cystic lung lesion composed of abnormal communicating airways; may present as a cystic or solid mass and cause respiratory distress in neonates.
symptoms_in_common: cystic/lucent lesion in a lung lobe on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: distinct systemic arterial feeder from the aorta (more characteristic of sequestration)
extrapulmonary pleural-based mass separate from lung parenchyma

data.description: A defect in the posterolateral diaphragm allowing abdominal contents to herniate into the thorax, causing pulmonary hypoplasia and respiratory distress.
symptoms_in_common: unilateral thoracic lucency with mass effect and mediastinal shift
symptoms_not_in_common: presence of a dedicated systemic arterial feeder to an intrathoracic mass
well-defined intrapulmonary lesion rather than bowel loops
lack of obvious intrathoracic bowel gas pattern

data.description: Air in the pleural space in a newborn, often presenting with acute respiratory distress and unilateral hyperlucency on chest radiograph.
symptoms_in_common: areas of increased lucency in one hemithorax
symptoms_not_in_common: visualized systemic arterial vessel supplying an intrathoracic mass
persistent soft‑tissue mass/opacity rather than free pleural air
vascularized lesion on Doppler/CT

data.description: Overexpansion of a lung lobe due to intrinsic or extrinsic bronchial obstruction, leading to respiratory distress in neonates.
symptoms_in_common: unilateral lobar hyperlucency with mass effect
symptoms_not_in_common: identification of a systemic arterial feeder from the aorta
solid or mixed cystic mass appearance rather than purely hyperinflated lung
pleural effusion

data.description: Infection or collapse of a lung segment/lobe causing focal opacification and respiratory distress in a newborn.
symptoms_in_common: focal unilateral opacity/atelectasis on chest imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: well-defined cystic lesion with systemic arterial supply
persistent large lucent mass effect
mediastinal shift primarily from a mass rather than consolidation

data.description: Severe, accelerated hypertension causing concentric smooth muscle and basement membrane proliferation in small arteries/arterioles (onion-skin lesions) leading to luminal narrowing and ischemic injury.
symptoms_in_common: Onion-skin concentric intimal thickening of small artery/arteriole on H&E (panel A/C)
Duplication/lamellation of basement membranes on silver stain (panel B)
Marked luminal narrowing/near-occlusion of small vessel
Perivascular ischemic-type changes without prominent inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of fibrinoid necrosis (more typical in malignant hypertension when acute)
No clinical data demonstrating markedly elevated blood pressure provided

data.description: A microvascular complication of systemic sclerosis characterized by abrupt severe hypertension and TMA-like vascular lesions, including onion-skin arteriolar changes and intimal proliferation.
symptoms_in_common: Duplication of basement membranes on special stain
Arteriolar luminal narrowing consistent with ischemic TMA-type injury
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical features of systemic sclerosis provided (e.g., skin thickening, Raynaud phenomenon)
No report of abrupt severe hypertension or rising creatinine

data.description: TMA encompasses disorders with endothelial injury leading to arteriolar/arterial intimal proliferation, basement membrane duplication, and possible thrombi; can be due to TTP, HUS, drugs, infections, or complement dysregulation.
symptoms_in_common: Concentric (onion-skin) intimal thickening of small vessels
Basement membrane duplication on silver stain
Marked luminal narrowing consistent with microangiopathic injury
symptoms_not_in_common: No overt thrombi identified in the provided sections (often present in TMA)
No systemic signs provided (e.g., thrombocytopenia, hemolysis, schistocytes)

data.description: Chronic antibody-mediated injury in renal allografts producing intimal fibroplasia of arteries and multilayering/duplication of basement membranes (double-contours), sometimes with onion-skin arteriolar changes.
symptoms_in_common: Intimal fibroplasia with onion-skin appearance in a small vessel
Duplication/lamellation of basement membranes (double-contour) on silver stain
Vascular narrowing consistent with chronic alloimmune injury
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of kidney transplantation provided
No mention of donor-specific antibodies or chronic rejection features

data.description: A prothrombotic autoimmune condition causing renal vascular lesions including TMA-like changes, fibrous intimal hyperplasia, and onion-skin arteriolar lesions.

Basement membrane duplication on special stain suggesting chronic endothelial injury

data.description: Congenital condition characterized by herniation of the cerebellar tonsils through the foramen magnum due to a small posterior fossa, causing crowding at the craniocervical junction and potential brainstem/medullary compression.

Apparent filling defect in a segmental pulmonary artery branch

symptoms_in_common: CT: peripheral parenchymal opacity abutting pleura
Possible pleural reaction adjacent to consolidation

symptoms_in_common: CT: peripheral wedge-like lesion consistent with infarct from embolic source
Lesion location along a distal pulmonary arterial branch

symptoms_in_common: Unilateral/mesial temporal lobe FLAIR hyperintensity on MRI
Possible enhancement in the affected temporal lobe
symptoms_not_in_common: No provided clinical symptoms such as fever, acute confusion, or seizures to corroborate typical presentation

data.description: Immune-mediated inflammation of the limbic system (often associated with antibodies such as LGI1, CASPR2, NMDA-R, Hu), presenting with subacute memory impairment, behavioral change, and seizures.
symptoms_in_common: Mesial temporal lobe hyperintensity on MRI
Limbic-predominant pattern without large territorial infarct appearance
Potential lack of marked mass effect
symptoms_not_in_common: No provided subacute memory/behavioral changes or seizures
No cancer history or autoantibody data provided
No bilateral involvement described (autoimmune limbic encephalitis often bilateral)

data.description: Transient MRI changes after prolonged seizures/status epilepticus due to cytotoxic/vasogenic edema, often involving mesial temporal structures, cortex, and hippocampus.
symptoms_in_common: Corticolimbic distribution compatible with peri-ictal changes
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical history of seizures/status epilepticus provided
No diffusion or perfusion data to support peri-ictal changes
No reversibility information (follow-up imaging not provided)

symptoms_not_in_common: No discrete mass or expansion clearly described

No diffusion restriction or vascular imaging data provided

data.description: On admission: marked leukocytosis with neutrophilia (WBC 24,000/mm³, 93.8% neutrophils), hyponatremia (124 mmol/L), hyperkalemia (6.0 mmol/L), hypochloremia (87 mmol/L), elevated BUN (30 mg/dL), mild hyperglycemia (158 mg/dL), low total protein (5.4 g/dL) and albumin (2.5 g/dL), markedly elevated AST (440 U/L), elevated ALT (63 U/L) and LDH (468 U/L), high CK (1915 U/L) and CK-MB (19.7 ng/mL), elevated troponin T (0.72 ng/mL), elevated fibrinogen (473 mg/dL), ferritin (2324 ng/mL), and soluble IL-2 receptor (3172 U/mL), with low iron (24 µg/dL) and low TIBC (108 µg/dL). Arterial blood gas on 100% oxygen showed severe acidemia and hypercapnia (pH 7.15, pCO₂ 88 mm Hg, pO₂ 45 mm Hg).

data.diagnosis: Severe bacterial pneumonia with sepsis and ARDS
data.description: A severe lung infection leading to systemic inflammatory response and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), characterized by shunt physiology, hypoxemia refractory to oxygen, and multiorgan stress.
symptoms_in_common: Severe hypoxemia despite 100% oxygen (pO2 45 mm Hg) suggesting shunt/ARDS
Elevated inflammatory markers (ferritin 2324 ng/mL, fibrinogen 473 mg/dL)
Low iron and low TIBC (anemia of inflammation pattern)
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe hypercapnia (pCO2 88 mm Hg) is less typical in ARDS (often low/normal CO2 early)
Markedly elevated CK (1915 U/L) and CK-MB (19.7 ng/mL)
Elevated troponin T (0.72 ng/mL)
Hyperkalemia (6.0 mmol/L)
Low total protein/albumin not specific to pneumonia

data.description: Skeletal muscle breakdown releasing intracellular contents (CK, potassium, myoglobin) leading to electrolyte disturbances and risk of acute kidney injury.
symptoms_in_common: AST markedly elevated with lesser ALT (AST 440 U/L > ALT 63 U/L)
Elevated BUN (30 mg/dL) suggesting possible renal stress
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe hypoxemia and hypercapnia (primary respiratory failure not typical for isolated rhabdomyolysis)
Marked leukocytosis with neutrophilia
Elevated troponin T and CK-MB (suggest additional cardiac involvement)
High ferritin and sIL-2 receptor (suggest systemic inflammation beyond isolated muscle injury)
Hyponatremia and hypochloremia not characteristic

data.diagnosis: Type 2 myocardial infarction (demand ischemia) or acute myocardial injury
data.description: Myocardial injury from supply–demand mismatch due to severe systemic illness (hypoxia, sepsis, respiratory failure), resulting in elevated cardiac biomarkers without primary coronary plaque rupture.
symptoms_in_common: Systemic stressors: severe hypoxemia and acidemia
Elevated fibrinogen and ferritin (acute phase reactants)
symptoms_not_in_common: Very high CK suggesting concurrent skeletal muscle injury
Severe hypercapnia is not a direct feature of myocardial injury
Hyponatremia and hyperkalemia are not typical of isolated demand ischemia
Low total protein/albumin not specific
Markedly elevated sIL-2 receptor not typical

data.description: A hyperinflammatory syndrome characterized by excessive immune activation leading to high ferritin, elevated soluble IL-2 receptor, liver enzyme elevations, and often cytopenias; can be triggered by infection.
symptoms_in_common: Low iron and low TIBC (inflammatory pattern)
symptoms_not_in_common: Leukocytosis with neutrophilia (HLH more often shows cytopenias)
Elevated fibrinogen (HLH often has low fibrinogen)
Severe hypercapnic respiratory failure not typical primary feature
Markedly elevated CK suggesting muscle injury
Hyperkalemia not characteristic of HLH itself

data.diagnosis: Ischemic hepatitis (shock liver) secondary to hypoxia/shock
data.description: Hepatocellular injury from reduced perfusion/oxygenation during shock or severe hypoxemia, causing transaminase and LDH elevations.
symptoms_in_common: Severe hypoxemia and acidemia consistent with hypoxic insult
AST and LDH elevation (pattern seen in ischemic injury)
symptoms_not_in_common: AST/ALT levels not in the classic thousands expected in ischemic hepatitis
Markedly elevated CK indicating skeletal muscle injury
Elevated troponin/CK-MB implying myocardial involvement
Hyponatremia and hyperkalemia not specific to ischemic hepatitis
Leukocytosis with neutrophilia suggests infection/sepsis as primary driver

data.description: Kanningar á laboratoriu vístu varandi hypofosfatemi við lágum normalum kalki, hægri alkaliskum fosfatasa og hægri PTH. data.diagnosis: Left-sided infective endocarditis (likely aortic valve) with systemic embolization
data.description: Infection of the cardiac endocardium, most often involving the aortic or mitral valve, producing friable vegetations that can embolize to the brain and spleen and may cause valvular destruction with aortic regurgitation.
symptoms_in_common: Mobile echogenic mass on aortic valve consistent with vegetation (echo finding)
Brain imaging lesion compatible with embolic infarct/abscess
Splenic hypoechoic lesions consistent with infarcts/abscesses (septic emboli)

data.description: Sterile fibrin-platelet vegetations on cardiac valves, often associated with malignancy or a hypercoagulable state, that can embolize systemically.
symptoms_in_common: Brain lesion compatible with embolic infarct
Splenic lesions consistent with infarcts from emboli
symptoms_not_in_common: Evidence of destructive valvulitis with significant aortic regurgitation (less typical in NBTE)
Features suggestive of infection such as abscess formation (not typical for sterile NBTE)

data.description: Benign intracardiac tumor (usually left atrial) that can fragment and embolize to the brain and systemic circulation.
symptoms_in_common: Systemic emboli to brain (cerebral lesion) and spleen
symptoms_not_in_common: Mass appears attached to valve rather than typical left atrial location
Significant aortic regurgitation (not characteristic of myxoma)
Vegetation-like appearance rather than a pedunculated atrial mass

data.description: Thrombus formation in the left atrium or appendage due to atrial fibrillation leading to systemic embolization to the brain and spleen.
symptoms_in_common: Cerebral lesion consistent with embolic infarct
symptoms_not_in_common: Distinct valvular vegetation on echocardiography (not typical of AF-related thrombus)
Significant aortic regurgitation (not expected consequence of AF alone)

data.description: Sterile verrucous vegetations on valves associated with systemic lupus erythematosus or antiphospholipid syndrome that can embolize.
symptoms_in_common: Valve-associated mass on echo compatible with sterile vegetation
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked aortic regurgitation from destructive lesions (less typical; LSE lesions often non-destructive)
Imaging features suggestive of abscess/sepsis rather than sterile vegetations
