data.description: A paraneoplastic dermatosis presenting with psoriasiform, violaceous, scaly plaques on acral sites (hands, feet, ears, nose) and nail dystrophy, most often associated with squamous cell carcinomas of the upper aerodigestive tract or esophagus. Cutaneous findings often precede cancer diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Violaceous-red scaly plaques on the dorsal hands and over knuckles
Hypermetabolic focus on PET/CT suggestive of an underlying malignancy
symptoms_not_in_common: Pruritus is not prominent (if present)
Facial/auricular involvement not shown
Palmoplantar hyperkeratosis not shown

data.description: An autoimmune inflammatory myopathy characterized by cutaneous findings (Gottron papules/sign on dorsal MCP/PIP joints, heliotrope rash) and proximal muscle weakness; in adults, it can be associated with malignancy.
symptoms_in_common: Scaly erythematous-to-violaceous plaques over the dorsal MCP/PIP joints (compatible with Gottron papules/sign)
Potential paraneoplastic process suggested by PET/CT hypermetabolic lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: No documented proximal muscle weakness
No heliotrope rash or periungual telangiectasias shown
No reported elevated muscle enzymes or myositis symptoms

data.description: A chronic immune-mediated skin disease with well-demarcated erythematous plaques and silvery scale, often on extensor surfaces; may involve nails with pitting or onycholysis.
symptoms_in_common: Erythematous scaly plaques on dorsal hands/fingers
Possible nail color changes consistent with psoriatic nail disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Classic well-demarcated plaques with thick silvery scale not clearly evident
Typical involvement of elbows, knees, scalp not shown
Association with a single hypermetabolic malignancy focus is not typical

data.description: Inflammatory dermatitis due to contact allergens or irritants; presents with erythema, scaling, fissuring, and pruritus on hands, often related to exposures.
symptoms_in_common: Erythematous scaly plaques on the hands
Distribution on dorsal hands and fingers
symptoms_not_in_common: Knuckle-centered, violaceous plaques are less typical
No clear vesiculation, oozing, or fissuring shown
Association with hypermetabolic malignancy on PET/CT is not typical

data.description: Dermatophyte infection of the hand presenting with annular scaly plaques or diffuse hyperkeratosis; often unilateral and associated with tinea pedis.
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesions appear symmetric and centered on knuckles rather than annular or unilateral
No involvement of palmar creases or classic active border
No mention of tinea pedis or onychomycosis
PET/CT finding of malignancy would be unrelated

data.description: A physeal disorder of the proximal femur in adolescents in which the femoral head (epiphysis) slips posteroinferiorly relative to the neck, often requiring in-situ pinning.
symptoms_in_common: Radiograph shows displacement/malalignment of the proximal femoral epiphysis relative to the neck
Widened and irregular proximal femoral physis
In-situ screw fixation across the proximal femoral physis (typical treatment finding)
Bilateral involvement risk suggested by contralateral fixation

data.diagnosis: Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease (avascular necrosis of the femoral head in childhood)
data.description: Idiopathic avascular necrosis of the capital femoral epiphysis in children leading to fragmentation, collapse, and remodeling of the femoral head.
symptoms_in_common: Hip pathology centered at the femoral head/epiphysis on radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Typical findings (crescent sign, fragmentation, sclerosis, and collapse of the epiphysis) are not evident
Slip through the physis and in-situ pinning are not typical features of Perthes disease
Age at presentation for Perthes is usually younger than typical SCFE patients

data.description: A spectrum of abnormalities in which the acetabulum and femoral head are maldeveloped, leading to subluxation or dislocation, commonly identified in infancy or early childhood.
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear superolateral displacement of the femoral head from the acetabulum as in DDH
Findings focus on physeal slip rather than acetabular dysplasia
Presence of transphyseal screws (typical of SCFE treatment), not DDH management
Age of typical DDH detection is infancy, not adolescence

data.diagnosis: Proximal femoral physeal fracture (Salter-Harris I of the proximal femur)
data.description: An acute traumatic separation through the proximal femoral growth plate that can mimic SCFE radiographically, often associated with acute pain and inability to bear weight.
symptoms_in_common: Pathology localized to the proximal femoral physis on imaging
Potential displacement at the growth plate
symptoms_not_in_common: Radiographs suggest chronic slip rather than an acute fracture line
Management in the images (in-situ pinning across the physis) is more typical for SCFE than for an acute traumatic physeal fracture
Lack of acute fracture cortical break or obvious fracture line

data.description: Blockage at or near the pylorus/duodenal bulb that prevents gastric emptying, leading to marked stomach dilation and a large intragastric air–fluid level.
symptoms_in_common: Large single air–fluid level in the stomach on erect radiograph
Transition near the pylorus/duodenal bulb suggested on CT
Relative absence of distal small-bowel dilatation
symptoms_not_in_common: No free intraperitoneal air seen (rules out perforation but not required)
No reported systemic symptoms provided (e.g., weight loss, vomiting), which are often present clinically

data.diagnosis: Pyloric channel scarring from peptic ulcer disease (cause of gastric outlet obstruction)
data.description: Chronic peptic ulcer disease can cause inflammation and fibrosis of the pyloric channel, narrowing the outlet and causing gastric retention.
symptoms_in_common: Marked gastric dilation with large air–fluid level
Apparent obstruction at the pylorus/duodenal bulb
Lack of small-bowel dilatation distal to the obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear ulcer crater or focal mural thickening identified on the provided images
No provided history of dyspepsia/ulcer symptoms or NSAID use

data.description: Twisting of the stomach along its axes (organoaxial or mesenteroaxial), which can acutely obstruct the gastroesophageal junction and/or pylorus, causing massive gastric distension and an air–fluid level.
symptoms_in_common: Severely distended stomach with a large air–fluid level
Imaging suggests proximal obstruction without distal small-bowel dilatation
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear CT signs of a twist (e.g., transition at both GE junction and pylorus, 'whirl' or 'beak' signs) documented
No paraesophageal hernia or intrathoracic stomach seen on the images provided

data.description: Compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the SMA and aorta leads to proximal duodenal and gastric dilation and delayed gastric emptying.
symptoms_in_common: Large, fluid-filled, dilated stomach suggesting proximal obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: No demonstration of a narrowed aortomesenteric angle or compressed third portion of the duodenum on the provided images
Typical clinical context (thin body habitus, recent weight loss) not provided

data.diagnosis: Duodenal obstruction from pancreatic head mass (e.g., pancreatic adenocarcinoma)
data.description: A mass in the pancreatic head can externally compress the duodenum, causing gastric outlet obstruction and gastric dilation.
symptoms_in_common: Marked gastric dilation with a large air–fluid level indicating gastric outlet obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: No pancreatic head mass or biliary ductal dilation evident on the provided CT images
No reported jaundice or weight loss

data.description: A lysosomal storage disorder caused by GALC deficiency leading to severe, symmetric demyelination that often involves the periventricular white matter, corticospinal tracts, posterior fossa, and the optic nerves/chiasm; typically presents in infancy but later-onset forms exist.
symptoms_in_common: Optic nerve/chiasm enlargement and T2 hyperintensity (optic pathway involvement)
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent ventriculomegaly/transependymal edema (if present), which is not a hallmark feature

data.description: An arylsulfatase A deficiency causing progressive demyelination with symmetric periventricular white matter changes that can show a tigroid pattern; classically spares subcortical U-fibers early and may involve corticospinal tracts.
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent optic nerve/chiasm enlargement (less typical)
Early cerebellar white matter involvement is less common than in Krabbe disease

data.description: A peroxisomal disorder with accumulation of very long-chain fatty acids causing inflammatory demyelination, classically beginning in the parieto-occipital periventricular white matter and splenium of the corpus callosum.
symptoms_in_common: Posterior periventricular white matter T2 hyperintensity
Symmetric confluent lesions around the bodies/splenium of the lateral ventricles
symptoms_not_in_common: Optic nerve/chiasm enlargement (not characteristic)
Early cerebellar white matter involvement is atypical
Lack of clear parieto-occipital predominance with advancing edge (if not seen)

data.description: An immune-mediated demyelinating disease characterized by disseminated CNS lesions, often periventricular (Dawson’s fingers), involving the optic nerves and brainstem/cerebellum; usually relapsing-remitting in young adults but can occur in pediatric patients.
symptoms_not_in_common: Highly symmetric confluent periventricular lesions (MS lesions are typically ovoid and asymmetric)
Diffuse optic nerve enlargement (MS optic neuritis usually lacks gross enlargement)
Patient age may be younger than typical MS onset

data.diagnosis: Periventricular leukomalacia (chronic hypoxic-ischemic white matter injury)
data.description: White matter injury of prematurity or early infancy due to hypoxia-ischemia, leading to periventricular gliosis and volume loss that can appear hyperintense on T2 with ventricular enlargement from parenchymal loss.
symptoms_in_common: Periventricular T2 hyperintensity adjacent to the lateral ventricles
Possible ventriculomegaly related to white matter loss
symptoms_not_in_common: Symmetric deep white matter confluent involvement beyond periventricular rims (PVL tends to be more focal and cystic in severe cases)
Optic nerve/chiasm enlargement (not expected)
Prominent cerebellar white matter involvement is unusual

data.diagnosis: Hepatoid/enteroblastic adenocarcinoma of the small intestine (AFP-producing)
data.description: A rare adenocarcinoma with hepatocellular or fetal enteroblastic differentiation that can arise in the gastrointestinal tract and often produces AFP and expresses GPC3; morphology is glandular/solid and epithelial markers are retained, with frequent CDX2 expression.
symptoms_not_in_common: SATB2 positivity (if present; hepatoid/enteroblastic tumors are often SATB2 negative)
CK7 negativity is variable (can be positive or negative)
CK20 negativity (some cases may show CK20 expression)

data.description: Malignant epithelial tumor arising from the small intestine, most commonly ileum/jejunum; typically shows glandular differentiation and intestinal markers like CDX2; CK7 and CK20 are variable.
symptoms_not_in_common: AFP positivity (uncommon in conventional SBA)
GPC3 positivity (uncommon)
Strong SATB2 positivity (more typical of colorectal origin if strong and diffuse)

data.diagnosis: Metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma to the small bowel
data.description: Secondary involvement of the small intestine by a colorectal primary, often via direct extension or metastasis; typically CDX2 and SATB2 positive and variably CK20 positive, usually CK7 negative.
symptoms_not_in_common: AFP positivity (not typical for colorectal adenocarcinoma)
GPC3 positivity (not typical)
CK20 negativity (many colorectal cancers are CK20 positive)

data.diagnosis: Metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma involving the small intestine
data.description: Spread of primary liver hepatocellular carcinoma to the gastrointestinal tract; tumors often express AFP and GPC3 and are keratin positive but typically lack intestinal transcription factors like CDX2.
symptoms_not_in_common: CDX2 positivity (not typical for HCC)
Jejunal primary mass without known liver primary
SATB2 positivity (if present, not expected in HCC)
EMA strong diffuse positivity is less characteristic than HepPar-1/Arginase-1 which are not provided

data.diagnosis: Metastatic yolk sac tumor (germ cell tumor) to the small intestine
data.description: A germ cell tumor that can rarely metastasize to GI tract; typically shows AFP and GPC3 positivity with germ cell markers such as SALL4 and sometimes OCT4.
symptoms_in_common: Epithelial cytokeratin positivity (can be present in yolk sac tumors)
symptoms_not_in_common: CDX2 positivity (unusual for yolk sac tumor)
OCT4 negativity (yolk sac tumors are usually OCT4 negative, but germ cell lineage often shows SALL4 positivity)
SALL4 negativity (expected to be positive in yolk sac tumor)
Location confined to jejunum without known gonadal/mediastinal primary

data.description: Severe anemia with hematocrit 17.5%, hemoglobin 5.7 g/dL, red-cell count 2.07 million/mm³, and elevated reticulocyte count 7.6%. Also noted leukocytosis (22,200/mm³) and low serum iron (19 µg/dL) with low total protein and globulin; coagulation studies were normal.

data.diagnosis: Meckel's diverticulum with ectopic gastric mucosa (bleeding Meckel)
data.description: A congenital ileal diverticulum that may contain ectopic gastric mucosa, leading to acid-induced ulceration and painless lower gastrointestinal bleeding; classically detected by Tc-99m pertechnetate scan showing a focus in the right lower quadrant that appears with and parallels gastric activity.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated reticulocyte count (7.6%) suggesting blood loss
Nuclear medicine scan showing focal uptake consistent with a bleeding source in the small bowel/right lower quadrant
symptoms_not_in_common: Low total protein and globulin (not typical unless concurrent protein loss or malnutrition)

data.diagnosis: Small-bowel angiodysplasia (vascular malformation) with active bleeding
data.description: Degenerative vascular malformations of the gastrointestinal tract that can cause intermittent or chronic bleeding, often identified on tagged red blood cell scans when bleeding is active.
symptoms_in_common: Nuclear scan compatible with an active GI bleeding focus
symptoms_not_in_common: Low total protein and globulin (not typical)
Leukocytosis (not a hallmark unless there is stress/inflammation)

data.diagnosis: Peptic ulcer disease with upper gastrointestinal bleeding
data.description: Erosions or ulcers in the stomach or duodenum that can bleed and cause acute or chronic iron-deficiency anemia; bleeding may be detected on nuclear scans if active.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated reticulocyte count indicating recent blood loss
Imaging consistent with an active GI bleed
symptoms_not_in_common: Focal uptake in the right lower quadrant (not typical for an upper GI source)
Low total protein and globulin (not characteristic)
Leukocytosis (not specific for peptic ulcer disease)

data.diagnosis: Crohn disease with gastrointestinal bleeding and protein-losing enteropathy
data.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease affecting any part of the GI tract, which can cause mucosal ulceration, bleeding, systemic inflammation, and protein loss.
symptoms_in_common: Severe anemia (often iron deficiency from chronic blood loss)
Low total protein and globulin (possible protein-losing enteropathy)
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated reticulocyte count is less typical unless there is recent acute blood loss
Nuclear scan showing a discrete focal bleeding spot (Crohn bleeding is often diffuse or ulcer-related rather than a single focal hotspot)

data.diagnosis: Small-intestinal tumor (e.g., gastrointestinal stromal tumor) with bleeding
data.description: Neoplasms of the small intestine, such as GISTs, can ulcerate and bleed, causing iron-deficiency anemia; active bleeding may be localized by tagged RBC scans.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated reticulocyte count suggesting ongoing blood loss
Nuclear scan compatible with a focal bleeding source
symptoms_not_in_common: Low total protein and globulin (not typical unless malnutrition or protein loss coexists)
Leukocytosis (not specific; may be reactive)

data.description: A pleural-based, round or wedge-shaped area of atelectasis that forms adjacent to pleural disease (effusion or thickening); vessels and bronchi curve toward the lesion (comet-tail sign).
symptoms_not_in_common: Central mucus plugging/bronchoceles
High-attenuation mucus within bronchi
Mosaic attenuation/expiratory air-trapping beyond the involved segment

data.description: A hypersensitivity reaction to airway colonization by Aspergillus leading to asthma exacerbations, central bronchiectasis, and high-attenuation mucoid impaction.
symptoms_not_in_common: Pleural-based rounded mass compatible with rounded atelectasis
Significant pleural effusion or fissural collections

data.diagnosis: Endobronchial tumor (e.g., carcinoid or obstructing neoplasm) with post-obstructive changes
data.description: A focal endobronchial lesion can obstruct a lobar/segmental bronchus causing distal mucus impaction, atelectasis, and recurrent infection.
symptoms_in_common: Segmental/lobar atelectasis distal to an obstructed bronchus
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse or central bronchiectasis typical of ABPA
Bilateral pleural/fissural fluid collections

data.diagnosis: Constrictive bronchiolitis (bronchiolitis obliterans) / small airways disease
data.description: Inflammatory and fibrotic narrowing of small airways causing air-trapping and mosaic attenuation, often more evident on expiratory CT.
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent central mucus plugging or high-attenuation mucus
Pleural-based rounded mass
Large pleural effusion/loculated fissural fluid

data.diagnosis: Pleural pseudotumor (loculated pleural effusion in a fissure)
data.description: A lenticular, mass-like collection of fluid trapped within a pleural fissure, often associated with heart failure or pleuritis; can mimic a tumor.
symptoms_in_common: Rounded/lenticular opacity along pleural surface or fissure
symptoms_not_in_common: Intrabronchial high-attenuation mucus plugs
Central bronchiectasis
Diffuse air-trapping/mosaic attenuation unrelated to pleural fluid

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection with reactivation in adults or older children, characteristically involving the apical/posterior segments of the upper lobes and forming cavitary necrotizing granulomas.

Multiple thick-walled cavities on CT with surrounding parenchymal destruction
Histology consistent with necrotizing granulomatous inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: No evident hilar lymphadenopathy
No miliary (diffuse micronodular) pattern seen
No documented constitutional symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss) provided

data.diagnosis: Necrotizing bacterial pneumonia with lung abscess (e.g., Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella, anaerobic aspiration)
data.description: Severe bacterial infection causing tissue necrosis and cavitation; may follow aspiration or hematogenous spread and can produce air–fluid–level cavities (abscesses).
symptoms_in_common: Focal lobar consolidation progressing to multiple cavitary lesions
Thick-walled cavities clustered within one lobe on CT
Histology showing marked acute inflammation and necrosis compatible with abscess formation
symptoms_not_in_common: Presence of well-formed granulomas (more typical of mycobacterial/fungal etiologies)
Predominant upper-lobe localization without clear dependent segment involvement
No reported acute systemic sepsis features provided

data.description: Opportunistic infection by Nocardia species causing cavitary consolidations and nodules, often in immunocompromised hosts and mimicking TB or fungal disease.
symptoms_in_common: Cavitary consolidation in the upper lobe on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No information suggesting immunosuppression
No mention of disseminated disease (e.g., brain abscesses)
Presence of well-formed granulomas is less typical for nocardiosis

data.description: A chronic fungal infection by Aspergillus spp. in structurally abnormal lungs, leading to slowly progressive upper-lobe cavities that may contain fungal balls.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple cavities with thick walls suggesting chronic process
symptoms_not_in_common: No pre-existing cavities or bronchiectasis documented
Histology described as necrotizing granulomatous inflammation without demonstration of fungal hyphae
No intracavitary mass (aspergilloma) visualized

data.description: ANCA-associated necrotizing vasculitis causing cavitating pulmonary nodules/masses, upper airway disease, and renal involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Cavitating parenchymal lesions on chest imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesions are predominantly confluent in a single upper lobe rather than multiple bilateral nodules
No clinical signs of upper airway disease or renal involvement provided
Granulomas appear infection-like rather than vasculitic features on provided histology

Mass-effect symptoms or solitary enhancing lesion on imaging (not provided)

CSF: only mild protein elevation (often higher)

data.description: X‑linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficient alpha‑galactosidase A leading to globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) accumulation in vascular endothelium, kidneys, and heart; presents with proteinuric kidney disease and concentric LV hypertrophy with conduction abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Left ventricular hypertrophy on ECG (high-voltage QRS with repolarization changes)
Concentric left ventricular wall thickening on echocardiography
Electron microscopy showing concentric lamellar myelin figures (“zebra bodies”) in podocytes, classic for Fabry

data.description: Genetic cardiomyopathy characterized by unexplained LV hypertrophy, often asymmetric, with myocyte disarray and potential for arrhythmias and sudden death.
symptoms_in_common: ECG showing LVH with repolarization abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Electron microscopy of kidney with zebra bodies (not a feature of HCM)
Podocyte storage inclusions/proteinuric kidney disease (HCM typically lacks renal storage pathology)

data.description: Systemic deposition of misfolded amyloid fibrils (AL or ATTR) in myocardium and other organs causing restrictive cardiomyopathy and often nephrotic-range proteinuria.
symptoms_not_in_common: ECG usually shows low voltage rather than high-voltage LVH
Kidney EM typically shows non-branching fibrils (8–12 nm), not lamellar zebra bodies

data.description: X‑linked vacuolar myopathy with cardiomyopathy due to lysosomal-associated membrane protein-2 deficiency; frequently presents with severe LV hypertrophy and pre-excitation on ECG.
symptoms_in_common: Marked LV hypertrophy on ECG and echocardiogram
symptoms_not_in_common: Kidney electron microscopy with zebra bodies (not typical; Danon shows autophagic vacuoles, not Gb3 lamellae)
Specific podocyte storage pattern and renal biopsy findings suggest Fabry rather than Danon

data.diagnosis: PRKAG2 syndrome (glycogen storage cardiomyopathy with pre-excitation)
data.description: Autosomal dominant disorder of cardiac AMP-activated protein kinase leading to glycogen accumulation, ventricular hypertrophy, and accessory pathway-mediated pre-excitation.
symptoms_in_common: ECG/echo evidence of significant LV hypertrophy
symptoms_not_in_common: Renal zebra bodies on EM (not a feature of PRKAG2 glycogenosis)
Renal storage disease/proteinuria not typical in PRKAG2
Specific lamellar inclusions favor Fabry rather than glycogen storage

data.diagnosis: Herpes zoster (cranial nerve distribution, trigeminal and possible facial nerve involvement)
data.description: Reactivation of varicella-zoster virus causing a painful, unilateral vesicular eruption in a dermatomal pattern; in the face it may involve trigeminal branches and can extend to the ear when multiple cranial nerves are involved, particularly in older or immunocompromised patients.
symptoms_in_common: Unilateral vesicular/erosive eruption on the face
Grouped vesicles and crusts on an erythematous base
Vesicles and bullae on the auricle/external ear
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral or symmetric distribution (not seen)
Generalized rash beyond the cranial dermatomes (not seen)

data.description: Varicella-zoster virus reactivation in the geniculate ganglion of the facial nerve leading to vesicles in the ear canal/pinna and potentially severe ear pain and facial nerve palsy; rash can extend to adjacent facial areas.
symptoms_in_common: Vesicles and bullae on the auricle/external ear
Unilateral clustered vesicles and crusts on the same side of the face
symptoms_not_in_common: Documented facial paralysis (not shown)
Hearing loss or vertigo (not provided)

data.description: Reactivation of varicella-zoster virus in the ophthalmic (V1) branch of the trigeminal nerve, producing a unilateral vesicular eruption on the forehead, scalp, and around the eye; can threaten ocular structures.

Erosions and crusting on an erythematous base
symptoms_not_in_common: Ear involvement with vesicles (not typical for isolated ophthalmic involvement)
Documented ocular findings such as conjunctivitis/keratitis (not provided)

data.description: Superficial bacterial skin infection (usually Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes) characterized by vesicles/pustules that rupture to form honey-colored crusts; bullous form produces larger flaccid bullae.
symptoms_in_common: Crusted erosions with exudate on the face
Vesicles/pustules that appear to rupture and crust
symptoms_not_in_common: Strict unilateral, dermatomal distribution (impetigo is usually non-dermatomal and can be multifocal or bilateral)
Prominent auricular canal vesicles/bullae (less typical)
Predominance in children rather than adults (patient appears older)

data.description: Autoimmune blistering disorder causing fragile intraepidermal (flaccid) bullae and erosions, often starting in the oral mucosa and spreading to the skin; can involve the face and scalp.
symptoms_in_common: Erosions and crusting on the face
Presence of bullae/vesicles that rupture easily
symptoms_not_in_common: Strictly unilateral, localized distribution (pemphigus is typically widespread and non-dermatomal)
Predominant ear canal involvement (unusual)
Absence of reported mucosal (oral) lesions

data.description: Focal dilatation of the abdominal aorta; risk of rupture increases with diameter >5.5 cm. Can occasionally compress adjacent structures.

Findings suggestive of urinary tract obstruction

CT image suggestive of obstructed collecting system; focal density in ureter possible for stone (arrow)

No reported classic colicky pain, hematuria, or dysuria

Hydronephrosis on ultrasound/CT without clear intraluminal mass
symptoms_not_in_common: Discrete ureteral calculus (if present) would be atypical for pure extrinsic compression
No bilateral hydronephrosis documented (compression may be unilateral or bilateral depending on anatomy)

Potential filling defect/soft tissue cause of obstruction considered on CT differential

Lack of reported hematuria or visible ureteral mass on provided images

rising BUN and creatinine with decreased eGFR (acute kidney injury)

diffuse pulmonary infiltrates consistent with ARDS

schistocytes and anemia from microangiopathic hemolysis

leukocytosis with left shift and toxic changes

severe lactic acidosis and shock picture

purpuric skin lesions/necrosis

data.diagnosis: Ischemic stroke from infective endocarditis (septic emboli)

symptoms_in_common: Echocardiogram shows LV apical thrombus compatible with aneurysm-related mural thrombus
MRA showing large-vessel (MCA) occlusion consistent with embolism
symptoms_not_in_common: No explicit history of prior myocardial infarction or LV aneurysm provided

data.diagnosis: Paradoxical embolic stroke via patent foramen ovale (PFO) with venous thromboembolism
data.description: A venous thrombus crosses a right-to-left shunt (e.g., PFO) and embolizes to the cerebral circulation, causing an acute ischemic stroke.
symptoms_in_common: Acute cortical infarct consistent with embolic mechanism
symptoms_not_in_common: Echocardiogram identifies an LV apical thrombus rather than a venous source
No evidence of DVT or right-to-left shunt provided

diagnoses.name: MELAS syndrome
diagnoses.title: MELAS - [Mitochondrial encephalopathy with lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes] syndrome

data.description: Laboratory findings on admission at two hospitals showed elevated liver tests and bilirubin: ALT 327/85 U/L, AST 104/267 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 172/150 U/L, and total bilirubin 5.8/6.7 mg/dL. Lipase was mildly elevated at 72 U/L. CA 19-9 was 73/79 U/mL. Hemoglobin, white-cell count, platelets, electrolytes, renal function, and albumin were within normal limits.

data.diagnosis: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (head of pancreas) with obstructive jaundice
data.description: Malignant epithelial tumor of the pancreatic ducts, often arising in the head where it causes extrahepatic biliary obstruction and cholestasis; CA 19-9 is frequently elevated and liver metastases can occur.
symptoms_in_common: Cholestatic liver-test pattern (markedly elevated alkaline phosphatase and total bilirubin)
Imaging evidence consistent with obstructive process at the pancreatic/biliary confluence (mass/stricture) and possible hepatic lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: Extremely high ALT and AST (transaminases are often only modestly elevated in purely obstructive jaundice)

data.description: Adenocarcinoma arising from the bile duct epithelium near the hepatic hilum, causing intrahepatic biliary obstruction and cholestasis; frequently presents with jaundice and elevated CA 19-9.
symptoms_in_common: Cholestatic liver-test pattern (very high alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin)
Possible hepatic lesions compatible with metastases
symptoms_not_in_common: Mildly elevated lipase
Markedly elevated ALT/AST (usually less dramatic in isolated cholangiocarcinoma)

data.description: Malignancy of the distal common bile duct that often mimics pancreatic head cancer by producing obstructive jaundice and elevated cholestatic enzymes; CA 19-9 may be high.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly elevated alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin
Imaging consistent with distal duct obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: Mild elevation of lipase
Very high transaminases (ALT/AST), which are not typically extreme in isolated distal cholangiocarcinoma

data.description: Adenocarcinoma of the gallbladder that can invade the biliary tree, producing obstructive jaundice and elevated cholestatic enzymes; tumor markers such as CA 19-9 may rise.
symptoms_in_common: Cholestatic pattern with high alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin
Imaging suggesting a biliary obstructive process
symptoms_not_in_common: Mild lipase elevation
Extremely high ALT/AST (less typical in purely obstructive patterns without concomitant hepatocellular injury)

data.description: Immune-mediated fibroinflammatory disease involving the pancreas and bile ducts, causing strictures and obstructive jaundice; can mimic pancreatic or biliary malignancy on imaging and may respond to steroids.
symptoms_in_common: Cholestatic liver-test abnormalities (high alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin)
Imaging that can show pancreatic/biliary strictures or mass-like lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: Very high CA 19-9 (typically normal or only mildly elevated in IgG4 disease)
Extremely high ALT/AST
Mildly elevated lipase is not characteristic but can occur

data.diagnosis: Choledocholithiasis with obstructive jaundice (with or without mild gallstone pancreatitis)
data.description: A gallstone obstructing the common bile duct causes extrahepatic cholestasis; transient pancreatic duct obstruction can mildly elevate lipase; CA 19-9 can rise in benign obstruction but usually normalizes after relief.
symptoms_in_common: High alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin consistent with obstruction
Mildly elevated lipase consistent with gallstone-related irritation/pancreatitis
symptoms_not_in_common: CA 19-9 as high as 7379 U/mL (rare in benign obstruction)
Persistently extreme ALT/AST elevations (benign obstruction typically causes modest transaminase rises unless acute biliary hepatitis)

data.description: Acute inflammation of the gallbladder typically caused by an obstructing gallstone in the cystic duct or neck, leading to gallbladder distension, wall thickening, edema, and possible pericholecystic fluid.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging shows gallstone at gallbladder neck/cystic duct (arrowed focus)
Pericholecystic inflammatory changes suggested on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Right upper quadrant pain (not provided)
Fever (not provided)
Leukocytosis (not provided)
Positive Murphy sign (not provided)

data.description: Stone(s) in the common bile duct causing partial or complete obstruction, potentially leading to jaundice, cholestatic liver enzyme elevation, and complications like cholangitis or pancreatitis.
symptoms_in_common: Possible obstructing calculus near gallbladder neck/infundibulum that could extend or migrate to CBD
symptoms_not_in_common: Jaundice (not provided)
Dark urine/pale stools (not provided)
Pruritus (not provided)
Cholestatic pattern on labs (elevated ALP/GGT, bilirubin) (not provided)

data.description: Impaction of a gallstone in the cystic duct or Hartmann’s pouch causing extrinsic compression of the common hepatic duct, leading to obstructive jaundice and recurrent inflammation; can progress to cholecystocholedochal fistula.
symptoms_in_common: Impacted stone at gallbladder neck/cystic duct on imaging
Adjacent biliary compression suggested by proximity to hepatic duct region
symptoms_not_in_common: Jaundice (not provided)
Recurrent right upper quadrant pain (not provided)
Cholestatic liver enzyme elevation (not provided)

data.description: Mechanical small bowel obstruction due to a large gallstone that has passed through a biliary-enteric fistula; often shows ectopic calcified stone, bowel obstruction, and sometimes pneumobilia.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal MRI with complex bowel loops; consideration of ectopic calcified focus
Possible cholecystoenteric fistula context from chronic gallstone disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Signs of small bowel obstruction (vomiting, abdominal distension, obstipation) (not provided)
Pneumobilia on imaging (not described)
Ectopic intraluminal stone distant from gallbladder (not clearly shown)

data.description: Malignancy of the gallbladder, often associated with longstanding gallstones and chronic inflammation; presents with mass replacing gallbladder, wall thickening, or polypoid lesions and can cause biliary obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Gallbladder with abnormal wall/contents on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Constitutional symptoms (weight loss, anorexia) (not provided)
Painless jaundice (not provided)
Mass replacing gallbladder or invasive features (not clearly described)
Liver invasion or lymphadenopathy (not provided)

data.description: A disruption of the patellar tendon leading to loss of continuity between the patella and tibial tubercle, often causing a high-riding patella (patella alta) and inability to actively extend the knee.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent patella alta on lateral knee X-ray
Normal-appearing tibiofemoral alignment without intra-articular fracture on AP view
symptoms_not_in_common: No obvious avulsion fragment from the inferior pole of the patella identified
Clinical findings such as extensor lag/inability to straight-leg raise not provided
Clear tendon discontinuity not directly visualized on plain radiograph

data.description: An avulsion of the tibial tubercle apophysis, typically in adolescents, due to forceful quadriceps contraction; can produce patella alta if the patellar tendon remains taut and pulls proximally.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent patella alta suggesting extensor mechanism disruption/traction
Age-typical pattern if patient is adolescent (implied by open apophyseal appearance on X-ray)
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear displaced fracture line or fragment at the tibial tubercle seen on the provided views
No obvious soft-tissue swelling specifically localized to the tibial tubercle
Lack of reported acute traumatic event

data.description: Acute lateral displacement of the patella that often spontaneously reduces; commonly in adolescents/young adults and associated with hemarthrosis and characteristic radiographic findings post-reduction.
symptoms_in_common: Knee effusion suggested by soft-tissue fullness on lateral view
Normal AP alignment post-reduction without fracture
Patellar position that may appear slightly high/maltracking on lateral
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear osteochondral fragment or medial patellar/femoral condyle avulsion visible
No lateralized patella on AP view
No reported history of a twisting injury or patellar instability symptoms

data.description: Overuse-related traction apophysitis of the tibial tubercle in adolescents, due to repetitive strain from the patellar tendon, leading to pain and possible prominence/fragmentation at the tubercle.
symptoms_in_common: Age-appropriate appearance of tibial tubercle apophysis (if adolescent)
Potential extensor mechanism stress suggested by subtle patellar malposition
symptoms_not_in_common: Patella alta is not a typical feature of Osgood–Schlatter disease
No clear fragmentation or swelling localized to the tibial tubercle on these views
Typically a chronic overuse presentation rather than acute radiographic change

data.description: A benign follicular developmental disorder characterized by numerous small dermal cysts that contain keratin and vellus hairs; lesions present as multiple tiny follicular papules, often brownish, sometimes with a central punctum.
symptoms_in_common: Brown round macules/papules with central keratin plug on dermoscopy
Distribution on scalp and upper extremities
Reflectance confocal microscopy showing a round cystic cavity with bright rim
Histology demonstrating dermal keratin-filled cysts containing vellus hairs with surrounding mild inflammation/granulomatous reaction
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent scalp involvement (EVHC more often on chest/trunk though can be widespread)
Apparent hyperpigmentation of many lesions (classically skin‑colored to yellow-brown)

data.description: A disorder with numerous sebum-filled dermal cysts arising from the pilosebaceous unit; lesions are usually soft, translucent to yellow papules/nodules and may exude oily fluid.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple folliculocentric papules on trunk/upper limbs
symptoms_not_in_common: Brown macules with central keratin plugs rather than translucent/yellow cysts
RCM and histology consistent with keratin-and-hair–containing cysts (not cyst walls with sebaceous lobules typical of steatocystoma)
Lack of oily fluid expression
Predominant small size (steatocystomas often larger, soft)

data.description: A common keratinization disorder with follicular plugging that produces rough, small keratotic papules on extensor surfaces.
symptoms_not_in_common: Discrete brown circular macules with central umbilication/plug rather than diffuse roughness
Presence of dermal cysts with vellus hairs on histology/RCM (not seen in keratosis pilaris)
Significant scalp involvement

data.description: Benign keratin-filled cysts derived from the follicular infundibulum; usually present as firm nodules with a central punctum.
symptoms_in_common: Histologic finding of a cyst lined by squamous epithelium with laminated keratin
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesions are typically larger solitary nodules, not numerous 1–3 mm papules
RCM/histology showing vellus hairs within cysts (more typical of EVHC)
Predominant distribution on scalp and upper arms rather than trunk or face

data.description: An uncommon follicular disorder with grouped patches of spiny hyperkeratotic follicular papules, often on extensor surfaces in adolescents and young adults.
symptoms_in_common: Grouped follicular papules on extensor arms
symptoms_not_in_common: Brown round lesions with central plugs instead of spiny projections
Evidence of dermal cysts with vellus hairs on imaging/histology
Widespread involvement including scalp, which is atypical

data.description: Protozoal infection (Leishmania) transmitted by sandflies that causes chronic papules or nodules that ulcerate with raised indurated borders and heal with atrophic scars; histology shows granulomatous inflammation with parasitized macrophages (amastigotes) early, later pauciparasitic granulomas.
symptoms_in_common: Single chronic ulcer on lower leg/ankle with necrotic base
Gradual evolution to crust and atrophic scar
Granulation tissue and granulomatous dermal infiltrate on histology
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of reported travel or sandfly exposure (often present)
No mention of satellite lesions or regional lymphadenopathy

data.description: A neutrophilic dermatosis characterized by rapidly progressive, painful ulcers with undermined violaceous borders, often following minor trauma and associated with systemic diseases such as IBD or arthritis.
symptoms_in_common: Painful-looking necro-ulcerative lesion on the leg
Improvement to a cribriform/atrophic scar with treatment
symptoms_not_in_common: Histology lacks dense neutrophilic infiltrate and sterile abscesses typical of pyoderma gangrenosum
No history of pathergy, systemic disease (IBD/arthritis), or multiple recurrent ulcers

data.description: A necrotizing cutaneous infection caused by M. ulcerans, producing painless, undermined ulcers on limbs due to mycolactone toxin; common in tropical regions and heals with scarring.
symptoms_in_common: Large necrotic ulcer on lower limb
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesion appears painful/inflamed rather than classically painless
Histology does not show extensive coagulative necrosis of fat with sparse inflammation typical of Buruli ulcer
No epidemiologic context (endemic area exposure) provided

data.description: A subcutaneous fungal infection caused by Sporothrix schenckii complex; inoculation leads to nodules that may ulcerate and can spread along lymphatics in a chain.
symptoms_in_common: Ulcerated nodule on distal lower extremity
Chronicity with gradual evolution and scarring
symptoms_not_in_common: No lymphangitic chain of nodules
Histology does not show cigar-shaped yeasts or mixed suppurative/granulomatous pattern typical for sporotrichosis
No history of gardening/trauma with plant material

data.description: A deeper bacterial infection of the epidermis/dermis presenting as punched-out ulcerations with overlying crusts on the lower legs; can heal with scars.
symptoms_in_common: Ulcer with necrotic/crusted center on lower leg
symptoms_not_in_common: Initial lesion appears larger and more indurated than typical ecthyma
Histology does not show primarily superficial epidermal ulceration with heavy neutrophilic crust and bacterial colonies
Prolonged course longer than usual for ecthyma

data.description: A malignant soft tissue sarcoma often composed of uniform spindle cells; characteristically expresses epithelial markers (cytokeratin, EMA) and TLE1, and is associated with the t(X;18)(p11;q11) SS18::SSX fusion.
symptoms_in_common: Highly cellular spindle cell proliferation on H&E
Prominent mitotic activity and nuclear atypia
Two immunostains showing strong, diffuse membranous/cytoplasmic positivity (compatible with epithelial marker-type staining)
symptoms_not_in_common: Lack of obvious biphasic pattern with distinct glandular structures
Predominant small round blue cell appearance in areas (less classic for monophasic spindle pattern)
No molecular confirmation of SS18::SSX fusion provided

data.description: A small round blue cell tumor of bone and soft tissue, typically showing diffuse membranous CD99 and NKX2.2 positivity and EWSR1 gene rearrangements.
symptoms_in_common: Sheets of small round to oval cells on H&E
High nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio with brisk mitoses
Diffuse strong membranous-type immunostaining pattern (could fit CD99)
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent strong epithelial-type immunoreactivity (if the positive stains are cytokeratin/EMA), which is atypical for classic Ewing sarcoma
Spindle-cell areas rather than purely uniform round cells

data.description: A malignant soft tissue tumor characterized by epithelioid and sometimes rhabdoid cells; commonly expresses cytokeratin and EMA, often CD34, with loss of INI1/SMARCB1.
symptoms_in_common: Epithelioid/rhabdoid-appearing cells with pleomorphism on H&E
Two immunostains with strong diffuse positivity consistent with epithelial marker expression
symptoms_not_in_common: Predominantly spindled architecture rather than classic nodular epithelioid pattern with central necrosis
No mention of INI1 loss or distal extremity/superficial location

data.description: A malignant skeletal muscle tumor of children and young adults; shows small round blue cells and myogenic marker positivity (myogenin, MyoD1, desmin).
symptoms_in_common: Small round blue cell morphology on H&E in parts
symptoms_not_in_common: Strong diffuse epithelial-type immunostaining rather than myogenic marker pattern
Absence of overt eosinophilic cytoplasm/cross-striations or alveolar pattern
Predominant spindle-cell component not typical

data.description: An aggressive spindle cell sarcoma arising from peripheral nerves; may show S100/SOX10 in a subset and often displays high cellularity and mitotic activity.
symptoms_in_common: Hypercellular spindle cell tumor on H&E
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse strong immunostaining resembling epithelial markers, which is unusual for classic MPNST
Lack of wavy nuclei or clear nerve association
Absence of patchy/weak S100 pattern information

diagnoses.title: Gastrointestinal stromal tumour of unspecified gastrointestinal sites

data.diagnosis: Solid pseudopapillary neoplasm (SPN) of the pancreas
data.description: A rare, low-grade malignant pancreatic tumor, typically in young women, characterized by a well-encapsulated solid-cystic mass with hemorrhage and pseudopapillary architecture; immunophenotype often vimentin+, CD10/PR+, nuclear beta-catenin, and usually negative or weak for chromogranin.
symptoms_in_common: Large, well-circumscribed pancreatic mass on CT
Heterogeneous solid and cystic components with hemorrhagic/necrotic areas
Microscopy showing uniform cells with pseudopapillary/solid sheets and low-grade cytology
Immunohistochemistry showing vimentin positivity; CD34 highlighting vessels rather than tumor cells
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked diffuse chromogranin positivity (not shown; would be atypical for SPN)
Overt infiltrative/desmoplastic growth pattern typical of ductal adenocarcinoma

data.description: Neoplasms arising from pancreatic neuroendocrine cells; often well-circumscribed and hypervascular, may be functional or nonfunctional, with solid nests/trabeculae on histology and strong neuroendocrine markers.
symptoms_in_common: Possible hemorrhagic/necrotic areas in larger tumors
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent pseudopapillary architecture (not typical for pNET)
Vimentin-dominant immunophenotype with lack of strong, diffuse chromogranin/synaptophysin staining
Encapsulated solid-cystic mass with extensive hemorrhage (more typical of SPN than pNET)

data.diagnosis: Acinar cell carcinoma of the pancreas
data.description: A malignant pancreatic exocrine tumor derived from acinar cells; often large and well-circumscribed with solid sheets and may show necrosis; expresses digestive enzymes (trypsin, chymotrypsin, BCL10).
symptoms_in_common: Large pancreatic mass that can be relatively well-circumscribed
Solid sheets of cells with areas of necrosis/hemorrhage
symptoms_not_in_common: Pseudopapillary architecture and encapsulation characteristic of SPN
Vimentin-dominant immunoprofile without acinar enzyme positivity
Typical acinar granular cytoplasm not evident

data.description: The most common pancreatic malignancy; typically ill-defined, infiltrative, desmoplastic mass causing ductal obstruction and often lacks a well-formed capsule.
symptoms_in_common: Pancreatic mass with necrosis can occur in large tumors
symptoms_not_in_common: Well-encapsulated, solid-cystic, hemorrhagic mass (unusual for ductal adenocarcinoma)
Absence of marked desmoplasia and infiltrative gland-forming pattern on histology
Immunophenotype not consistent with ductal lineage

data.diagnosis: Extragastrointestinal gastrointestinal stromal tumor (EGIST) adjacent to pancreas
data.description: A rare mesenchymal tumor similar to GIST but arising outside the GI tract (e.g., retroperitoneum/pancreatic vicinity); typically spindle/epithelioid cells, often c-KIT/DOG1 positive, and may be well-circumscribed with hemorrhage.
symptoms_in_common: Large, well-circumscribed mass in pancreatic region
CD34 positivity confined to vessels can be seen in background tissues (though tumor CD34/c-KIT positivity would be expected in EGIST)
symptoms_not_in_common: Pseudopapillary architecture and vimentin-dominant profile without c-KIT/DOG1 expression
Location clearly intrapancreatic with encapsulation typical of SPN rather than a true EGIST

data.description: Benign clonal epidermal proliferations showing epidermolytic hyperkeratosis on histology. They present as multiple skin-colored to brown, verrucous papules that often cluster and coalesce in intertriginous sites such as the axillae and neck.
symptoms_in_common: Numerous brown to gray verrucous papules
Hyperkeratotic surface consistent with histology showing epidermal hyperkeratosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Widespread involvement beyond flexures (not seen)
Ulceration or marked erosion (not shown)

data.description: Velvety hyperpigmented thickening of intertriginous skin, commonly associated with insulin resistance or internal malignancy in select cases.
symptoms_not_in_common: Discrete verrucous/papillomatous papules and pedunculated lesions (less typical; AN is usually smoother and velvety rather than verrucous papules)
Clustered keratotic papules coalescing into cobblestone plaques (more suggestive of papillomatous/epidermolytic lesions)
Evidence of systemic signs of insulin resistance or malignancy (not provided)

data.description: Disorder of keratinization characterized by hyperpigmented, slightly verrucous papules and plaques that become confluent centrally and reticulated peripherally, classically on the central chest and upper back, sometimes neck.
symptoms_not_in_common: Predominant axillary involvement (CRP more often affects central chest/back)
Prominent discrete, pedunculated papules (less typical)
Reticulated peripheral pattern not clearly evident

data.description: Common benign epidermal tumors presenting as 'stuck-on,' verrucous, hyperkeratotic papules or plaques; can be pigmented and occur in large numbers in older adults.
symptoms_not_in_common: Predominant flexural distribution (seborrheic keratoses are usually widespread on trunk/face rather than confined to axilla/neck)
Cobblestoned, confluent plaques in intertriginous folds (less typical for classic SK)

data.description: Autosomal dominant keratinization disorder with greasy, hyperkeratotic papules in seborrheic and flexural areas; histology shows acantholysis and dyskeratosis (corps ronds and grains).
symptoms_not_in_common: Greasy, malodorous, crusted papules with erosions (not evident)
Typical nail changes and mucosal involvement (not shown)
Onset usually earlier in life (age not provided), and histology would show acantholysis/dyskeratosis rather than purely epidermolytic hyperkeratosis

data.description: Benign, expansile, blood-filled cystic lesion of bone that can be primary or occur secondarily within another tumor; common in adolescents and young adults and can present with multiloculated, septated cavities and fluid–fluid levels.
symptoms_in_common: Expansile lytic lesion of the right iliac bone
Multiloculated 'bubbly' appearance with internal septations on CT/MRI
FDG uptake on PET (can be mild to moderate in ABCs)
symptoms_not_in_common: Pelvic/iliac location is less common than long bones
If the patient is older than early adulthood, age would be atypical for primary ABC
Marked FDG avidity would be less typical than in malignant mimics

data.diagnosis: Giant cell tumor of bone (GCT) with secondary ABC change
data.description: Locally aggressive benign tumor of osteoclast-like giant cells, typically in skeletally mature patients; can undergo secondary aneurysmal change producing fluid–fluid levels.
symptoms_in_common: Lytic expansile lesion with internal septations
Fluid–fluid levels suggest secondary ABC change
Hypermetabolism on PET is common in GCT
symptoms_not_in_common: Classic GCT favors epiphyseal/subarticular locations; iliac wing location is less typical
Absence of a dominant solid soft-tissue component would be atypical
Marked cortical breach or soft-tissue mass not clearly evident, which may be seen in aggressive GCTs

data.description: High-grade malignant osteosarcoma variant composed of blood-filled spaces that can mimic ABC radiologically but shows malignant solid components and produces osteoid.
symptoms_in_common: Expansile lytic lesion with fluid–fluid levels
symptoms_not_in_common: Overt aggressive periosteal reaction or a large soft-tissue mass is not obvious on provided images
No clear mineralized osteoid matrix seen
Patient’s lesion appears well contained with thin cortex for the most part, less typical for a high-grade malignancy

data.diagnosis: Chondromyxoid fibroma (often with secondary ABC-like change)
data.description: Rare benign cartilage-derived tumor characterized by lobulated chondromyxoid tissue; usually metaphyseal in long bones but can occur in the pelvis and may show internal septations and occasional cystic change.
symptoms_in_common: Bone scan uptake can be present
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent fluid–fluid levels are not classic and suggest secondary ABC change
Typical chondroid matrix calcification ('rings and arcs') is not evident
Marked FDG uptake would be atypical for a purely benign CMF

data.description: Localized proliferation of monoclonal plasma cells, most often in axial skeleton; presents as a lytic lesion and is typically FDG-avid, sometimes preceding multiple myeloma.
symptoms_in_common: Lytic lesion involving the iliac bone
Pelvic location is common for axial skeletal lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiloculated cystic architecture with fluid–fluid levels is atypical
Internal septal enhancement pattern is less characteristic
Bone scan may show variable uptake, sometimes low; here there is notable uptake

Autoimmune disorder characterized by fluctuating axial and proximal limb stiffness and stimulus-triggered spasms; commonly associated with high-titer anti-GAD antibodies and continuous motor unit activity on EMG.
symptoms_in_common: Classical SPS phenotype with axial stiffness and spasms
Severe gait impairment requiring wheelchair prior to treatment
EMG showing continuous motor unit activity
Partial/insufficient response to IVIG and plasmapheresis
symptoms_not_in_common: None clearly discordant with classic SPS in this case

data.diagnosis: Progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity and myoclonus (PERM)
data.description: A severe form within the stiff-person spectrum featuring diffuse rigidity, myoclonus, brainstem involvement, autonomic dysfunction, and encephalopathy; often associated with glycine receptor antibodies.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported encephalopathy or brainstem/autonomic signs
Anti-GAD positive rather than anti-glycine receptor
EMG findings fit SPS but PERM typically has broader CNS signs

data.description: Peripheral nerve hyperexcitability disorder causing continuous muscle fiber activity, cramps, fasciculations, and stiffness; often autoimmune (VGKC-complex antibodies).
symptoms_in_common: Continuous motor unit activity on EMG
Chronic course with potential immunotherapy response
symptoms_not_in_common: Predominantly distal muscle involvement expected, not classic axial stiffness
Anti-GAD positivity is not typical (VGKC-complex/CASPR2 more typical)
Blink reflex hyperexcitability is less characteristic
Classical SPS phenotype better explains gait dependence and axial rigidity

data.description: Acute neurotoxin-mediated disorder causing generalized rigidity and painful spasms due to disinhibition of motor neurons.
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute/subacute presentation expected, not 8-year chronic course
No wound or infection history provided
Anti-GAD antibodies and autoimmune markers not expected
Improvement after HSCT and prior IVIG/plasmapheresis not typical of tetanus

data.description: Stiff-person phenotype associated with malignancy (often breast or small-cell lung) and antibodies such as anti-amphiphysin; may include focal stiff-limb syndrome.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported malignancy or paraneoplastic features
Anti-GAD positive rather than anti-amphiphysin
Blink reflex hyperexcitability and EMG findings fit classic anti-GAD SPS better

data.description: A chronic, granulomatous large-vessel vasculitis primarily affecting the aorta and its major branches, leading to stenosis, occlusion, or aneurysm; most common in younger women.
symptoms_in_common: Large-vessel stenosis on angiography (common carotid origin narrowing)
Ischemic scalp ulcer/necrosis due to reduced external carotid circulation
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported constitutional symptoms (fever, weight loss, limb claudication)
No reported pulse deficits or blood pressure asymmetry

data.description: An immune-mediated granulomatous vasculitis of medium and large arteries in adults, often involving the extracranial branches of the carotid, causing ischemic complications.
symptoms_in_common: Ischemic scalp ulcer/necrosis (from compromised scalp blood supply)
Large-vessel involvement possible (carotid/subclavian stenosis on imaging)
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported new headache, jaw claudication, or visual symptoms
No reported polymyalgia rheumatica symptoms
Age not stated; typical disease occurs in patients >50 years

data.diagnosis: Atherosclerotic carotid artery disease with external carotid ischemia
data.description: Atherosclerotic narrowing of the carotid arteries can reduce perfusion to the scalp via external carotid branches, rarely causing ischemic scalp ulcers in severe disease.
symptoms_not_in_common: No mention of vascular risk factors (e.g., diabetes, smoking, hyperlipidemia)
Scalp ischemic ulcers are uncommon without widespread peripheral vascular disease

data.description: A necrotizing vasculitis of medium-sized arteries causing ischemia and infarction in multiple organs; cutaneous manifestations include ulcers and nodules.
symptoms_not_in_common: Large-vessel carotid stenosis is not typical
No reported systemic involvement (renal, neurologic mononeuritis multiplex, abdominal pain)
No livedo reticularis or nodules reported

data.diagnosis: Infectious necrotic ulcer (e.g., ecthyma gangrenosum or necrotizing soft tissue infection)
data.description: Rapidly progressive necrotic skin lesions due to invasive bacterial infection (often Pseudomonas) leading to black eschar and ulceration, typically in immunocompromised hosts.
symptoms_not_in_common: Carotid artery stenosis on imaging is not characteristic
No reported systemic sepsis signs (fever, hypotension, neutropenia)
Single localized lesion without widespread involvement is less typical

data.description: A parasitic infection caused by Leishmania donovani complex, characterized by reticuloendothelial system involvement with amastigotes (Leishman-Donovan bodies) in macrophages; typically presents with prolonged fever, weight loss, hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia, and hypergammaglobulinemia.

data.description: Laboratory data showed, 1 month before admission, mild leukopenia (WBC 3810/μL), mild thrombocytopenia (207,000/μL normal? actually platelets 207k normal) and otherwise unremarkable labs. By hospital day 5, anemia had worsened (hemoglobin 9.4 g/dL), thrombocytopenia persisted (99,000/μL), renal function improved (creatinine 1.07 mg/dL), but liver tests worsened (AST 407 U/L, ALT 138 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 510 U/L, bilirubin 2.6 mg/dL), with persistent high D-dimer (3457 ng/mL) and hypoalbuminemia (2.3 g/dL).

data.description: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia with thrombocytopenia, often triggered by Shiga-toxin; classically involves acute kidney injury and elevated LDH.
symptoms_not_in_common: Peripheral smear with intraerythrocytic ring forms (not typical; schistocytes expected)
CSF Wright stain with ring forms (not typical)
Low albumin/total protein (nonspecific)
No reported renal dysfunction (typical in HUS but not described here)

data.diagnosis: Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) secondary to severe infection
data.description: Systemic activation of coagulation causing consumption of platelets and clotting factors; leads to elevated D-dimer, thrombocytopenia, and anemia from hemolysis.
symptoms_in_common: Low albumin/total protein (can occur in severe systemic illness)
symptoms_not_in_common: Peripheral smear with intraerythrocytic ring forms (not a feature of DIC)
CSF Wright stain showing intraerythrocytic ring forms (not explained by DIC)
Basophilic stippling (not typical)
Polychromasia and anisocytosis alone do not define DIC

data.diagnosis: Uterine leiomyosarcoma with pulmonary and hepatic metastases
data.description: An aggressive malignant tumor arising from uterine smooth muscle that often presents with a pelvic mass and can spread hematogenously to lungs and liver.
symptoms_in_common: Pelvic mass with coarse calcifications consistent with uterine origin
Multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules (cannonball-type) on CT
Hepatic mass suggestive of metastatic deposit
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms provided (e.g., abnormal uterine bleeding, pelvic pain) to support a uterine primary

data.diagnosis: Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (choriocarcinoma) with lung metastases
data.description: A malignant trophoblastic tumor that arises after pregnancy events and commonly metastasizes hematogenously to the lungs and sometimes liver.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple pulmonary nodules consistent with hematogenous spread
Possible hepatic lesion compatible with metastasis
symptoms_not_in_common: Calcifications within the pelvic mass are less typical for choriocarcinoma
No history provided of recent pregnancy or elevated beta-hCG

data.description: A rare condition where histologically benign uterine leiomyomas are associated with slow-growing extrauterine nodules, most commonly in the lungs, usually in women with current or prior uterine fibroids or after hysterectomy.
symptoms_in_common: Calcified pelvic mass compatible with uterine leiomyoma
symptoms_not_in_common: Large hepatic mass is uncommon in BML
No history provided of prior uterine surgery or hormonal context

data.description: A malignant ovarian tumor that often presents with a pelvic mass and can spread transcoelomically and hematogenously to the liver and, less commonly, to the lungs.
symptoms_in_common: Hepatic lesion compatible with metastatic disease
Pulmonary nodules possible with advanced disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Coarse calcifications and uterine-centered appearance favor leiomyoma rather than classic ovarian carcinoma imaging
Lack of ascites or peritoneal implants on the provided images

data.diagnosis: Disseminated granulomatous infection (e.g., tuberculosis or histoplasmosis)
data.description: Systemic infections that can cause multiple pulmonary nodules and hepatic lesions; pelvic calcifications could be incidental fibroid.
symptoms_in_common: Hepatic lesion that could represent granuloma
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent calcified uterine mass suggests a structural gynecologic lesion rather than infectious etiology
No systemic infectious symptoms provided (fever, weight loss, night sweats)

data.description: Laboratory results on presentation showed severe hypokalemia (K 1.8 mmol/L) with mild hyperglycemia (141 mg/dL), elevated alkaline phosphatase (156 U/L), AST (54 U/L), ALT (67 U/L), total bilirubin (1.3 mg/dL), and aldolase (9.9 U/L). Venous blood gas showed acidemia with pH 7.29 and PCO2 56 mm Hg. Other electrolytes, renal function, albumin, INR, calcium, magnesium, and creatine kinase were within reference range or near normal.

data.diagnosis: Graves disease with thyrotoxic periodic paralysis (TPP)
data.description: Autoimmune hyperthyroidism causing diffuse thyroid hypervascularity and hyperfunction. In susceptible patients (often men of Asian ancestry), hyperthyroidism can precipitate TPP, characterized by profound intracellular potassium shift and severe hypokalemia, sometimes with muscle weakness and hypercapnic respiratory acidosis.
symptoms_in_common: Severe hypokalemia (K 1.8 mmol/L) consistent with TPP
Elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin (can occur in thyrotoxicosis)
Elevated aldolase (muscle involvement in periodic paralysis)
Ultrasound showing diffusely enlarged, markedly hypervascular thyroid ('thyroid inferno')
Histology compatible with diffuse hyperplasia and lymphoid aggregates seen in Graves
Acidemia with elevated PCO2 (possible hypoventilation from TPP-related muscle weakness)
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal creatine kinase (CK is often normal or mildly elevated in TPP, but marked elevation would be more typical for myonecrosis)
Hypercapnic respiratory acidosis is not a typical baseline feature of Graves without TPP

data.diagnosis: Toxic multinodular goiter with thyrotoxicosis-induced periodic paralysis
data.description: Autonomously functioning thyroid nodules produce excess thyroid hormone, leading to thyrotoxicosis that can trigger hypokalemic periodic paralysis.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin (possible in thyrotoxicosis)
Acidemia with elevated PCO2 potentially from paralysis
symptoms_not_in_common: Ultrasound shows diffuse marked hypervascularity rather than multinodularity typical of toxic multinodular goiter
Histology in the case appears diffuse rather than nodular hyperplasia

data.description: Early or fluctuating phase of autoimmune (Hashimoto) thyroiditis where hormone leakage causes transient thyrotoxicosis; in rare cases this can precipitate hypokalemic periodic paralysis.
symptoms_in_common: Severe hypokalemia (possible if thyrotoxicosis triggers periodic paralysis)
Elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin (can be seen in thyrotoxic states)
Histology may show lymphoid aggregates compatible with autoimmune thyroiditis
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked diffuse hypervascularity on ultrasound favors Graves rather than Hashitoxicosis (which is often less vascular or even hypovascular)
Scalloped colloid and diffuse hyperplasia are more characteristic of Graves than Hashimoto
Acidemia with hypercapnia is not typical unless periodic paralysis with respiratory involvement occurs

data.description: Autonomous aldosterone secretion leads to renal potassium wasting and hypertension; classically causes metabolic alkalosis and mild hyperglycemia.
symptoms_not_in_common: Acidemia with elevated PCO2 (primary hyperaldosteronism typically causes metabolic alkalosis, not acidemia)
Elevated aldolase (not typical)
Elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin (not typical)
Thyroid ultrasound showing diffuse hypervascularity is unrelated
Histology pointing to diffuse thyroid disease is not explained by this diagnosis

data.description: A congenital split or cleft of the uvula that is usually benign and asymptomatic; may occur in isolation or be associated with submucous cleft palate.
symptoms_in_common: Normal-appearing mucosa without erythema or ulceration
No obvious tonsillar enlargement or exudate
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain or sore throat
Fever
Dysphagia or odynophagia
Airway compromise

data.description: A congenital defect where the muscles of the soft palate are cleft under intact mucosa; often associated with a bifid uvula and can cause velopharyngeal insufficiency.
symptoms_in_common: Normal-appearing surface mucosa (defect can be submucosal)
symptoms_not_in_common: Hypernasal speech
Nasal regurgitation during swallowing
Recurrent otitis media or eustachian tube dysfunction
Feeding difficulties in infancy

data.description: A benign squamous papilloma, often HPV-associated, presenting as a pedunculated or lobulated exophytic lesion on the uvula.
symptoms_in_common: Lesion with intact mucosa and no ulceration
symptoms_not_in_common: Rapid growth
Bleeding or ulceration
Multiple lesions elsewhere in the oral cavity
Voice changes or foreign body sensation

data.description: Enlargement of the uvula that can be idiopathic or related to chronic irritation, snoring, or obstructive sleep apnea.
symptoms_not_in_common: Snoring or sleep-disordered breathing
Gagging, choking, or sensation of a lump in the throat
Recurrent sore throat
Obesity or other risk factors for OSA

data.description: Inflammation and swelling of the uvula due to infection, allergy, trauma, or irritants; can cause sore throat and airway symptoms.
symptoms_not_in_common: Erythema and marked edema
Sore throat or odynophagia
Fever or systemic symptoms
Drooling, muffled voice, or respiratory distress

data.description: Focal protrusion or extrusion of intervertebral disc material that can compress adjacent nerve roots, causing back pain and radicular symptoms.
Narrowing of the spinal canal and/or neural foramina, often due to degenerative changes, leading to compression of neural elements and possible neurogenic claudication.
Age-related degeneration of intervertebral discs and adjacent vertebral structures, which can cause chronic low back pain and contribute to disc height loss and osteophyte formation.
Anterior slippage of a vertebral body due to facet joint and disc degeneration, potentially causing nerve root compression and back/leg symptoms.

data.diagnosis: Cauda equina syndrome (secondary to severe lumbar stenosis or large disc herniation)
data.description: Compression of the cauda equina nerve roots, typically from a large central disc herniation or severe stenosis; presents with back pain, bilateral leg symptoms, saddle anesthesia, and bowel/bladder dysfunction; a surgical emergency.

diagnoses.name: Intervertebral disc prolapse
diagnoses.title: Intervertebral disc degeneration without prolapsed disc with determinant

data.diagnosis: Infective endocarditis with septic emboli and intracranial mycotic aneurysms
data.description: Bacterial infection of cardiac valves causing showering of septic emboli to the brain and lungs; may form distal (mycotic) cerebral aneurysms and septic pulmonary emboli.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple acute cortical/subcortical diffusion-restricted brain lesions consistent with embolic infarcts
Small cortical lesion with a hypointense rim compatible with a distal mycotic aneurysm
Catheter/MR angiography showing distal branch aneurysms/irregular vessels
Chest CT with multiple peripheral lung nodules, some cavitary, suggestive of septic pulmonary emboli
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported fever or bacteremia
No mention of heart murmur or valvular disease
No peripheral stigmata of endocarditis reported

data.diagnosis: Septic pulmonary emboli from right-sided endocarditis (e.g., tricuspid) with secondary brain emboli
data.description: Right-sided valvular infection (often in IV drug use) leading to embolization of infected thrombi to lungs and occasionally paradoxical/systemic emboli causing brain infarcts/abscesses.
symptoms_in_common: Chest CT showing multiple peripheral cavitary nodules consistent with septic pulmonary emboli
Brain MRI demonstrating multifocal acute embolic-appearing lesions
Cerebral angiography demonstrating distal aneurysmal changes that can occur with septic emboli
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of IV drug use or indwelling catheter provided
No reported signs of right-sided heart infection (e.g., tricuspid regurgitation, septic shock)
No documented intracardiac shunt to allow systemic embolization if purely right-sided disease

data.diagnosis: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (Wegener) with pulmonary nodules and CNS vasculitis
data.description: ANCA-associated small to medium vessel vasculitis causing necrotizing granulomas in the respiratory tract and kidneys; can cause cavitary lung nodules and CNS ischemia/aneurysms due to vasculitis.
symptoms_in_common: Chest CT with multiple nodules including cavitary lesions
Multifocal brain ischemic lesions consistent with vasculitic/embolic phenomena
Angiographic distal vessel irregularities possibly reflecting vasculitis
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported chronic sinusitis, nasal ulcerations, or otitis
No hematuria or renal involvement noted
No laboratory data (ANCA) provided

data.diagnosis: Primary angiitis of the central nervous system (PACNS)
data.description: Idiopathic vasculitis confined to the CNS causing multifocal ischemia and aneurysmal changes without systemic involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Angiography with multifocal distal vessel irregularities/beading
Multiple acute cortical/subcortical infarcts on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Presence of multiple cavitary pulmonary nodules, which are not typical for PACNS
No reported headaches, subacute cognitive decline, or CSF inflammatory findings

data.diagnosis: Disseminated fungal infection (e.g., invasive aspergillosis) with pulmonary nodules and CNS involvement
data.description: Angioinvasive fungal disease starting in lungs and spreading hematogenously to the brain, producing infarcts, hemorrhagic lesions, or mycotic aneurysms.
symptoms_in_common: Chest CT showing multiple peripheral nodules with cavitation typical of angioinvasive fungi
Brain MRI with multifocal diffusion-restricted lesions (angioinvasion causing infarcts)
Angiographic distal aneurysms compatible with mycotic aneurysms
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of immunosuppression, neutropenia, or transplant reported
No fever or respiratory symptoms described
No serum fungal markers (e.g., galactomannan) provided

data.description: A malignant lymphoproliferative disease characterized by FDG-avid lymphadenopathy, often involving mediastinal nodes; can generate a hypercoagulable state and provoke venous thromboembolism.
symptoms_in_common: Intense FDG uptake in multiple lymph node stations (neck/mediastinum/hilar regions) on PET
Pulmonary embolism (filling defects in pulmonary arteries) consistent with cancer-associated thrombosis
Peripheral pulmonary opacities compatible with pulmonary infarcts
symptoms_not_in_common: Granulomatous inflammation on histology (Hodgkin lymphoma typically shows Reed–Sternberg cells rather than granulomas)

data.description: A multisystem granulomatous disease characterized by noncaseating granulomas and symmetric FDG-avid hilar/mediastinal lymphadenopathy; can involve liver and other organs.
symptoms_in_common: PET-avid bilateral mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy
Granulomatous inflammation on histology compatible with sarcoid-type granulomas
symptoms_not_in_common: Pulmonary embolism (not typical, though sarcoidosis can rarely be associated with VTE)
Large bulky nodal masses (sarcoidosis nodes are usually enlarged but not mass-like)
Any caseating necrosis if present (would argue against classic sarcoid)

data.description: Mycobacterial infection causing caseating granulomatous inflammation with FDG-avid lymph nodes; may present with mediastinal/hilar lymphadenopathy and can lead to hypercoagulability and PE.
symptoms_in_common: Granulomatous inflammation on histology (particularly if necrotizing)
Pulmonary embolism possible in TB due to inflammation-related thrombosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of cavitary parenchymal lung lesions on CT
Lack of systemic constitutional symptoms in the provided description (fever, weight loss, night sweats not specified)

data.diagnosis: Metastatic solid malignancy with cancer-associated thrombosis
data.description: Disseminated malignancy (e.g., lung, GI, or unknown primary) with nodal metastases that are FDG-avid and a propensity to cause venous thromboembolism.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple FDG-avid nodal sites on PET
Pulmonary embolism with peripheral pulmonary infarcts on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Granulomatous histology (metastatic carcinoma typically shows malignant epithelial cells, not granulomas)
Lack of a discrete primary tumor identified on the provided imaging

data.description: ANCA-associated necrotizing granulomatous vasculitis that affects the respiratory tract and can be FDG-avid; vasculitis can predispose to thrombosis and pulmonary emboli.
symptoms_in_common: Granulomatous inflammation on histology (necrotizing granulomas possible)
FDG uptake in thoracic structures (active vasculitic/granulomatous lesions can be PET-avid)
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of classic GPA parenchymal findings such as cavitating pulmonary nodules or upper airway/sinus disease on the provided images
No mention of renal involvement or hematuria
