A genetic disorder of impaired osteoclast-mediated bone resorption leading to abnormally dense but brittle bones and narrowed marrow spaces. Adult forms often present with diffuse osteosclerosis, high BMD, and characteristic radiographic changes.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly increased bone mineral density (T-score +7.1 lumbar spine, +5.1 femoral neck)
Diffuse pelvic and proximal femoral osteosclerosis on radiograph
Histology suggesting thickened trabeculae with reduced marrow space
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported history of pathologic fractures or cranial nerve compression (often seen in osteopetrosis)
No described anemia or marrow failure features (can occur in osteopetrosis)

data.description: A focal disorder of accelerated bone remodeling with excessive resorption followed by disorganized formation; later stages show dense, enlarged, sclerotic bone.
symptoms_in_common: Very high BMD compatible with excessive bone formation
Pelvic involvement on imaging (pelvis is a common site)
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent diffuse, uniform osteosclerosis rather than focal, patchy lesions typical of Paget disease
No mention of bone enlargement, deformity, or elevated alkaline phosphatase, which are common in Paget disease

data.diagnosis: Sclerostin pathway disorders (sclerosteosis/van Buchem disease) or LRP5 high bone mass
data.description: Inherited high bone mass syndromes due to reduced sclerostin activity or activating LRP5 mutations, causing increased osteoblast activity and markedly elevated BMD.
symptoms_in_common: Extremely elevated BMD at spine and hip
Histology consistent with increased lamellar bone
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported craniofacial overgrowth or syndromic features (often present in sclerosteosis/van Buchem)
Adult-onset presentation would be less typical for congenital high bone mass syndromes

data.description: Chronic excessive fluoride exposure leads to increased bone formation, osteosclerosis, and ligament/tendon calcifications; often presents with high BMD and dense bones on imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse osteosclerosis of pelvis on radiograph
Histologic appearance of dense, thickened trabeculae
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of fluoride exposure or dental changes reported (typical in fluorosis)
No mention of ligamentous calcifications or joint stiffness commonly seen in fluorosis

data.description: Metastatic spread from osteoblastic tumors can cause widespread osteosclerosis, particularly in the axial skeleton and pelvis, elevating measured BMD.
symptoms_in_common: Increased pelvic bone density on radiograph
High areal BMD that could be driven by osteoblastic activity
symptoms_not_in_common: Radiograph suggests uniform sclerosis rather than multifocal patchy lesions typical of metastases
No systemic or oncologic history provided (pain, weight loss, elevated PSA), which usually accompanies osteoblastic metastases

data.description: Marked hypernatremia and hyperchloremia on presentation (sodium 164 mmol/L, chloride 124 mmol/L), with elevated serum osmolality (334 mOsm/kg). Mild azotemia with creatinine normalizing over 3 days. Additional abnormalities included low testosterone, low LH/FSH, low free T4, low cortisol, elevated prolactin, and elevated cholesterol/LDL. Urine showed low sodium (64 mmol/L) and elevated osmolality (314 mOsm/kg). CSF was clear with mild pleocytosis and elevated protein; cytology showed no malignant cells, with oligoclonal immunoglobulin heavy-chain pattern and polyclonal T-cell receptor pattern.

Immune-mediated inflammation of the pituitary and stalk that can involve the anterior and posterior pituitary, leading to hypopituitarism, hyperprolactinemia (stalk effect), and central diabetes insipidus; MRI often shows stalk thickening/enhancing sellar–suprasellar lesion; CSF may show mild inflammatory changes.
symptoms_in_common: Low testosterone with low LH/FSH (central hypogonadism)
Hypernatremia and elevated serum osmolality consistent with untreated central diabetes insipidus/adipsic DI
Urine osmolality lower than serum (relative water diuresis)
Visual field deficits consistent with chiasmal compression
CSF mild pleocytosis and elevated protein (inflammatory profile)
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked hyperchloremia (not specific but not typical hallmark)
Elevated LDL cholesterol (secondary to hypothyroidism rather than the primary disease)
Mild azotemia that normalized (likely from dehydration rather than primary hypophysitis feature)

data.description: Granulomatous inflammation from sarcoidosis that can infiltrate the pituitary, stalk, and hypothalamus causing panhypopituitarism and central diabetes insipidus; MRI may show enhancing lesions and stalk thickening; CSF often shows inflammatory changes with elevated protein and pleocytosis.
symptoms_in_common: Central hypogonadism (low testosterone with low LH/FSH)
Hypernatremia/elevated serum osmolality suggesting central diabetes insipidus or adipsic DI
Visual field deficits from chiasmal involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of reported systemic sarcoidosis signs (e.g., pulmonary, skin, uveitis)
No elevated ACE level reported
Urine sodium not particularly low and only modestly dilute urine (CSF/MRI and labs fit better than urine pattern)

data.description: Epithelial tumor of the sellar/suprasellar region that commonly causes compression of the optic chiasm and hypothalamic–pituitary dysfunction; can lead to hypopituitarism and diabetes insipidus, often seen on MRI as a suprasellar mass.
symptoms_in_common: Visual field deficits compatible with chiasmal compression
Low pituitary hormones (central hypogonadism, hypothyroidism, secondary adrenal insufficiency)
Possible central diabetes insipidus with hypernatremia
symptoms_not_in_common: CSF pleocytosis and oligoclonal immunoglobulin pattern (not typical for craniopharyngioma)
Marked hyperprolactinemia is usually mild (stalk effect) rather than prominent
No mention of cystic components or calcifications (classic for craniopharyngioma)

data.description: A benign pituitary tumor >1 cm that can compress the optic chiasm and impair pituitary function; stalk compression can raise prolactin; anterior hypopituitarism is common.
symptoms_in_common: Central hypogonadism, hypothyroidism, and secondary adrenal insufficiency
Visual field defects suggesting chiasmal compression
symptoms_not_in_common: Central diabetes insipidus and marked hypernatremia are uncommon with adenomas
CSF pleocytosis and elevated protein are not expected
Posterior pituitary/stalk inflammatory-appearing enhancement is less typical for adenoma

data.description: A CNS germ cell tumor that often arises in the suprasellar region, frequently causing central diabetes insipidus and hypopituitarism in younger patients; may show an enhancing stalk/hypothalamic mass.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated prolactin due to stalk involvement
Enhancing suprasellar/pituitary stalk lesion on MRI
Visual field defects from chiasmal compression
symptoms_not_in_common: CSF cytology negative for malignant cells
No tumor markers (beta-HCG/AFP) reported
Patient age not specified; germinomas are classically in adolescents/young adults, less common in older adults
CSF oligoclonal heavy-chain pattern is more suggestive of inflammation than neoplasm

data.description: A benign cardiac tumor most often arising from the interatrial septum in the left atrium, typically pedunculated and mobile, which can prolapse through the mitral valve and cause obstructive or embolic symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Transesophageal echocardiogram shows a pedunculated, mobile mass attached to the interatrial septum in the left atrium
Mass prolapsing toward/through the mitral valve orifice (ball-valve effect)
symptoms_not_in_common: ECG with progressive PR prolongation and dropped QRS complexes (Mobitz I AV block)
Premature atrial contractions

data.diagnosis: Left atrial thrombus (often in setting of atrial fibrillation or atrial enlargement)
data.description: An intracardiac clot, most commonly forming in the left atrial appendage, associated with stasis (e.g., atrial fibrillation) and risk of systemic embolization.
symptoms_in_common: Echocardiographic visualization of an intracavitary left atrial mass
Mobile echodensity within the left atrium compatible with thrombus
symptoms_not_in_common: Pedunculated, septal-based stalk typical of myxoma rather than thrombus
ECG evidence of Mobitz I AV block (not typical for thrombus)
Premature atrial contractions (not required for diagnosis)

data.diagnosis: Infective endocarditis with mitral valve vegetation
data.description: Infection of the endocardial surface leading to friable vegetations on valves; can cause regurgitation, emboli, and systemic signs of infection.
symptoms_in_common: Oscillating echodense mass near/at the mitral valve apparatus consistent with a vegetation
Mobile mass that may prolapse into the mitral orifice
symptoms_not_in_common: Lack of reported fever, bacteremia, or systemic infectious signs
ECG Mobitz I AV block (more typical with aortic root abscess than isolated mitral vegetations)
Premature atrial contractions (nonspecific)

data.diagnosis: Second-degree atrioventricular block, Mobitz type I (Wenckebach)
data.description: Progressive prolongation of the PR interval culminating in a nonconducted P wave, resulting in grouped beating; often due to AV nodal conduction delay.
symptoms_in_common: Dropped QRS complexes following grouped beats
Regularly irregular rhythm pattern consistent with Wenckebach
symptoms_not_in_common: Left atrial mass on echocardiography (not a typical feature of Mobitz I)
Premature atrial contractions (may coexist but not required)

data.description: Early atrial depolarizations originating outside the sinus node, producing early P waves with different morphology and a noncompensatory pause; commonly benign but can cause palpitations or trigger other arrhythmias.
symptoms_in_common: ECG beats with early P waves of abnormal morphology
Noncompensatory pause following premature atrial beat
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive PR prolongation with dropped beats (points to concurrent Mobitz I rather than isolated PACs)
Left atrial mass on echocardiography (unrelated to PACs)

data.diagnosis: Infantile-onset Pompe disease (Glycogen storage disease type II)
data.description: Autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA) deficiency leading to glycogen accumulation, especially in cardiac and skeletal muscle; presents in infancy with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and progressive weakness.
symptoms_in_common: markedly reduced/absent acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA) bands on western blot indicating enzyme deficiency

data.description: X-linked dominant lysosomal/autophagic disorder due to LAMP2 deficiency, causing early hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, skeletal myopathy, and sometimes cognitive issues.
symptoms_in_common: cardiomegaly on chest X-ray (consistent with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy)
symptoms_not_in_common: reduced or absent GAA protein on western blot (not typical; GAA is normal in Danon disease)

data.description: Autosomal recessive defect in carnitine transporter (SLC22A5) leading to impaired fatty acid oxidation; can present in infancy with cardiomyopathy and hypoketotic hypoglycemia.
symptoms_not_in_common: reduced or absent GAA protein on western blot (not expected; enzyme is normal)
lack of documented hypoglycemia or metabolic decompensation

data.diagnosis: Glycogen storage disease type III (Cori/Forbes disease)
data.description: Autosomal recessive debranching enzyme (AGL) deficiency causing glycogen accumulation in liver and muscle; can lead to hepatomegaly and cardiomyopathy in some patients.
symptoms_in_common: cardiomegaly on chest X-ray (possible hypertrophic cardiomyopathy)
symptoms_not_in_common: reduced or absent GAA protein on western blot (not typical; GAA levels are normal)
lack of reported hepatomegaly or hypoglycemia

data.description: Cardiomyopathy due to defects in mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation; may present in infancy with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and multi-system features.
symptoms_not_in_common: reduced or absent GAA protein on western blot (not typical; GAA is unaffected)
no documented multisystem mitochondrial features (e.g., lactic acidosis, neuromuscular signs)

data.description: Anemia leve progresiva respecto al año anterior, con hematocrito del 35,6% al 30,9% y hemoglobina de 12,0 a 10,6 g/dL, con microcitosis en empeoramiento (MCV 81,5 a 75 fL). Marcadores inflamatorios elevados antes del ingreso y al ingreso, incluyendo VS 41–66 mm/h y PCR 3,0–8,3 mg/dL. Al ingreso, los glóbulos blancos eran 7.800/mm³ con diferencial normal, plaquetas 366.000/mm³, reticulocitos 3,0%, PT 14,4 seg/INR 1,2, LDH 517 U/L y ferritina 470 ng/mL. Los anticuerpos contra Borrelia burgdorferi fueron negativos.

Una neoplasia maligna de células B precursoras que puede presentarse con afectación de la médula ósea (LLA) y/o masas extranodales de tejido blando (LBL). Frecuentemente asociada con LDH elevada y marcadores inflamatorios sistémicos; La PET/TC suele mostrar lesiones intensamente hipermetabólicas.
symptoms_in_common: Marcadores inflamatorios elevados (VS 41–66 mm/h, CRP 3,0–8,3 mg/dL)
Masas hipermetabólicas en PET/TC en tejidos blandos/órganos
Recuento de blancos normal o casi normal posible en la enfermedad temprana
symptoms_not_in_common: Microcitosis (MCV 75 fL), que es poco común en la anemia leucémica (normalmente normocítica)
Ferritina 470 ng/mL (puede estar elevada pero no específica)
La reticulocitosis (3,0%), mientras que la insuficiencia medular suele causar bajos reticulocitos

data.description: Anemia hipoproliferativa provocada por citocinas inflamatorias que causan secuestro de hierro y eritropoiesis deteriorada. Típicamente normocítica o ligeramente microcítica y acompañada de ferritina elevada y marcadores inflamatorios.
symptoms_in_common: Plaquetas normales a altas (366.000/μL) suelen observarse en inflamación
symptoms_not_in_common: LDH marcadamente elevado (517 U/L), no típico sin un proceso concurrente
Las masas hipermetabólicas en la PET/TC sugieren una enfermedad focal más que una inflamación sistémica aislada
Reticulocitosis (3,0%)—TOCC suele ser hipoproliferativa con retics bajos

data.description: Anemia por hierro insuficiente que lleva a una reducción de la síntesis de hemoglobina; clásicamente microcítica e hipocrómica.
symptoms_not_in_common: Ferritina alta (debería ser baja en caso de deficiencia aislada de hierro)
PCR/VS elevadas (no es típico salvo inflamación simultánea)
LDH elevada (no es típica)
Masas hipermetabólicas en la imagen (no relacionadas con la deficiencia aislada de hierro)
Reticulocitosis (3,0%): la deficiencia de hierro suele tener retics bajos hasta que se trata

data.description: Destrucción mediada por el sistema inmunitario de glóbulos rojos que conduce a anemia con LDH elevado, bilirrubina indirecta y reticulocitosis.
symptoms_not_in_common: Microcitosis (AIHA, normalmente normocítica)
Ferritina alta, no característica
Los glóbulos blancos normales y las plaquetas de alta normalidad no apuntan específicamente a AIHA

data.description: Infección bacteriana del músculo esquelético que causa abscesos focales; se presenta con dolor/hinchazón localizada, inflamación sistémica y puede mostrar masas ávidas de FDG en PET/TC.

Appearance of cortical/medullary continuity with the parent bone
Bone scan shows focal increased uptake at the lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: Skin changes or inflammation (not evident)
Neurologic deficits or severe pain (not reported)

data.diagnosis: Myositis ossificans (heterotopic ossification) of the hip region
data.description: Benign, reactive ossification within soft tissues, typically following trauma; shows a zonal pattern of maturation from the periphery inward.
symptoms_in_common: Palpable mass in the soft tissues near the hip
Bone scan uptake can be present in active lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: Typical history of recent trauma or repetitive injury (not provided)
Zonal maturation pattern with peripheral ossification and central lucency on imaging (not described)
Lack of clear separation from bone (this lesion appears attached/pedunculated from bone, which is atypical)

data.description: A low-grade surface osteosarcoma arising from the outer periosteal surface, often presenting as a densely ossified, lobulated mass attached to bone.
symptoms_in_common: Exophytic, ossified mass attached to bone surface on CT
Bone scan uptake at the lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: Usually presents with pain and progressive enlargement (not reported)
Often shows aggressive or infiltrative features (not evident)
Common site is the posterior distal femur rather than the iliac crest (location atypical)

data.description: A rare malignant soft tissue tumor that produces osteoid without direct attachment to bone.
symptoms_in_common: Large ossified mass in the soft tissues
Bone scan uptake can occur due to osteoid production
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesion typically not attached to bone (this mass appears connected by a stalk to the pelvis)
Often painful and rapidly enlarging (not reported)
Usually occurs in older adults with aggressive imaging features (not evident here)

data.description: A benign lipomatous tumor that contains areas of calcification or ossification, usually arising in soft tissues and presenting as a painless mass.
symptoms_in_common: Painless, palpable mass near the hip
Imaging shows a lobulated mass with calcified/ossified components
symptoms_not_in_common: Direct bony attachment with cortex/medullary continuity (expected in osteochondroma, not lipoma)
Intense focal bone scan uptake (not typical for simple lipomas)
Predominantly fatty composition on CT/MRI (not described)

data.diagnosis: Lateral tibial plateau fracture (Schatzker II: split-depression)
data.description: An intra‑articular fracture of the lateral tibial plateau characterized by a vertical split with depression of the articular surface, typically from a valgus/axial load injury.
symptoms_in_common: X‑ray showing depressed lateral tibial plateau articular surface
Fracture line in lateral plateau with step-off
symptoms_not_in_common: No significant joint space narrowing typical of chronic degenerative disease
No generalized osteophyte formation

data.diagnosis: Pure depression fracture of the lateral tibial plateau (Schatzker III)
data.description: Impaction injury causing depression of the lateral tibial plateau articular surface without a large split component; often from axial load with valgus stress.
symptoms_in_common: X‑ray suggestion of lateral plateau articular surface depression
symptoms_not_in_common: Clear large vertical split component (would favor Schatzker II)
Medial plateau involvement

data.description: Chronic degenerative joint disease characterized by cartilage loss, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and joint space narrowing, leading to mechanical knee pain.
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute traumatic fracture line is not typical
Articular surface depression of the lateral tibial plateau is not typical
Lack of marked joint space narrowing and marginal osteophytes on the X‑ray

data.description: Avulsion of the tibial insertion of the anterior cruciate ligament, often from hyperextension or pivoting injury; common in adolescents but can occur in adults.
symptoms_not_in_common: X‑ray does not clearly show an avulsed tibial spine fragment
Presence of lateral tibial plateau articular depression favors plateau fracture instead

data.description: Mesenchymal tumor of the gastrointestinal tract derived from interstitial cells of Cajal; most are KIT or PDGFRA driven and show KIT (CD117) and/or DOG1 positivity.
symptoms_in_common: Spindle-cell neoplasm in gastric wall/submucosa on H&E
KIT gene mutation on sequencing chromatogram

data.description: Benign (leiomyoma) or malignant (leiomyosarcoma) smooth muscle tumors that can occur in the stomach and present as spindle-cell masses.
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse strong KIT (CD117) positivity (usually negative in smooth muscle tumors)
DOG1 positivity (not typical)
Presence of KIT gene mutation (not expected in smooth muscle tumors)

data.description: Benign nerve sheath tumor of the stomach characterized by S100 positivity and spindle cells with peripheral lymphoid cuffs.
symptoms_not_in_common: Strong KIT (CD117) positivity (schwannomas are typically KIT-negative)
DOG1 positivity (not typical)
KIT gene mutation (not typical for schwannoma)
Absence of classic S100-diffuse positivity and nuclear palisading in the provided findings

data.description: Locally aggressive myofibroblastic proliferation that can involve the mesentery or abdominal wall and mimic GI spindle tumors; usually shows nuclear beta-catenin mutations/positivity.
symptoms_in_common: Bland spindle-cell proliferation with fascicular pattern
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse KIT (CD117) and DOG1 positivity (not typical)
KIT gene mutation (not typical)
Lesion appears intramural gastric rather than mesenteric/abdominal wall
Lack of reported nuclear beta-catenin staining/mutation

data.description: Mesenchymal tumor characterized by NAB2-STAT6 fusion and STAT6 nuclear positivity; can rarely present in the abdomen and mimic other spindle-cell tumors.
symptoms_not_in_common: Strong KIT (CD117) and DOG1 positivity (SFTs are typically negative)
KIT gene mutation (not expected in SFT)
No mention of STAT6 nuclear positivity or characteristic staghorn vasculature

data.description: Short stature and low body weight with triangular face, prominent forehead, small chin, hypoplastic nasal alae/thin nostrils, large mouth with thin downturned lips, low-set ears, and deeply set eyes. Also delayed teething with microdontia, delayed bone age, thin wrinkled skin with visible vessels, lipoatrophy, delayed speech development, and insulin resistance; intelligence was within normal range.

A rare autosomal-dominant disorder (often due to PIK3R1 variants) characterized by short stature, partial lipodystrophy, characteristic triangular face with prominent forehead and deep-set eyes, delayed teething, and insulin resistance.
symptoms_in_common: large mouth with thin downturned lips
thin, wrinkled skin with visible vessels
symptoms_not_in_common: low-set ears
hypoplastic nasal alae/thin nostrils

data.description: An imprinting/epigenetic growth disorder causing severe pre- and postnatal growth restriction, relative macrocephaly, and triangular face; development is often normal or mildly delayed.
symptoms_in_common: short stature and low body weight
symptoms_not_in_common: lipoatrophy
thin wrinkled skin with visible vessels
insulin resistance
delayed teething with microdontia
deeply set eyes
hypoplastic nasal alae/thin nostrils

data.description: A laminopathy (LMNA or ZMPSTE24 variants) with mandibular and clavicular hypoplasia, acro-osteolysis, partial lipodystrophy, progeroid appearance, short stature, and metabolic complications including insulin resistance.
symptoms_in_common: thin, wrinkled skin with visible vessels
symptoms_not_in_common: deeply set eyes (not typical)
hypoplastic nasal alae/thin nostrils
lack of clavicular/acral abnormalities noted
delayed bone age not characteristic pattern

data.description: A classic progeroid laminopathy with severe postnatal growth failure, lipodystrophy, thin skin with prominent veins, characteristic facies, and progressive vascular disease; intellect is typically normal.
symptoms_in_common: thin, wrinkled skin with visible vessels
symptoms_not_in_common: insulin resistance (not typical early)
delayed teething with microdontia
deeply set eyes (progeria usually has prominent eyes)
lack of alopecia/joint contractures reported

data.description: A rare autosomal-recessive disorder with near-total absence of adipose tissue from birth, muscular appearance, hepatomegaly, and early severe insulin resistance; facial dysmorphism is usually mild.
symptoms_not_in_common: triangular face with prominent forehead
deeply set eyes
delayed teething with microdontia
thin wrinkled skin with visible vessels (degree not typical)
small chin
delayed bone age
short stature (height often normal early childhood)
